title.zh: 卷七十 志第四十六 選舉二
title.raw: 卷七十 志第四十六 選舉二 Volume 70 Treatises 46: Selection of Officials 2

sentences.zh: 科目者，沿唐、宋之舊，而稍變其試士之法，專取四子書及《易》、《書》、《詩》、《春秋》、《禮記》五經命題試士。

translations.literal: The examination track followed the Tang and Song precedents, yet altered somewhat the method of testing scholars, taking exclusively the Four Books and the Five Classics—the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Record of Rites—as topics for examining scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The civil examination system carried forward Tang and Song precedent but reshaped how candidates were tested: questions were drawn solely from the Four Books and the Five Classics—the Book of Changes, Book of Documents, Book of Odes, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 蓋太祖與劉基所定。

translations.literal: This was established by the founding emperor and Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: These rules were laid down by the founding emperor and Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 其文略仿宋經義，然代古人語氣為之，體用排偶，謂之八股，通謂之制義。

translations.literal: Its essays imitated in outline the Song "exposition of the classics," yet were written in the voice of the ancients, structured in parallel couplets, called the eight-legged essay, and generally termed regulated compositions.
translations.idiomatic: The essays loosely followed the Song form of classical exposition, but candidates wrote in the voice of the ancients, in parallel couplets—hence the name "eight-legged essay," or more generally "regulated composition."

sentences.zh: 三年大比，以諸生試之直省，曰鄉試。

translations.literal: At the triennial great comparison, students were examined in the metropolitan province and each province; this was called the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years, at the great triennial comparison, degree students were examined in the capital province and in each province—the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 中式者為舉人。

translations.literal: Those who passed were called Presented Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed were styled Presented Scholars (juren).

sentences.zh: 次年，以舉人試之京師，曰會試。

translations.literal: The following year, Presented Scholars were examined at the capital; this was called the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they were examined in the capital—the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 中式者，天子親策於廷，曰廷試，亦曰殿試。

translations.literal: Those who passed were personally examined by the Son of Heaven in court; this was called the palace examination, also termed the hall examination.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed then faced the emperor's questions in court—the palace examination, also called the hall examination.

sentences.zh: 分一、二、三甲以為名第之次。

translations.literal: They were divided into the first, second, and third cohorts to fix the order of names and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates were ranked in three cohorts—the first, second, and third.

sentences.zh: 一甲止三人，曰狀元、榜眼、探花，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: The first cohort had only three men, called Top Graduate, Second Graduate, and Third Graduate, and were granted jinshi with immediate appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The first cohort held only three places—the Top Graduate, Second Graduate, and Third Graduate—who received the degree of jinshi with immediate appointment.

sentences.zh: 二甲若干人，賜進士出身。

translations.literal: The second cohort had a certain number of men and were granted jinshi status.
translations.idiomatic: A set number in the second cohort received the degree of jinshi.

sentences.zh: 三甲若干人，賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: The third cohort had a certain number of men and were granted status equivalent to jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: A set number in the third cohort received the degree of tong jinshi—jinshi by equivalence.

sentences.zh: 狀元、榜眼、探花之名，制所定也。

translations.literal: The names Top Graduate, Second Graduate, and Third Graduate were fixed by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The titles Top Graduate, Second Graduate, and Third Graduate were established by statute.

sentences.zh: 而士大夫又通以鄉試第一為解元，會試第一為會元，二、三甲第一為傳臚云。

translations.literal: Yet scholars and officials also commonly called the first in the provincial examination Jieyuan, the first in the metropolitan examination Huiyuan, and the first in the second or third cohort Chuandu.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials also commonly called the top provincial pass Jieyuan, the top metropolitan pass Huiyuan, and the leader of the second or third cohort Chuandu.

sentences.zh: 子、午、卯、酉年鄉試，辰、戌、醜、未年會試。

translations.literal: Provincial examinations were held in the years of zi, wu, mao, and you; metropolitan examinations in the years of chen, xu, chou, and wei.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examinations fell in the years of the Rat, Horse, Rabbit, and Rooster; metropolitan examinations in the years of the Dragon, Dog, Ox, and Goat.

sentences.zh: 鄉試以八月，會試以二月，皆初九日為第一場，又三日為第二場，又三日為第三場。

translations.literal: The provincial examination was in the eighth month, the metropolitan in the second; in each, the ninth day was the first session, three days later the second, and three days after that the third.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial examination was held in the eighth month, the metropolitan in the second. Each had three sessions on the ninth day, then three days later, then three days after that.

sentences.zh: 初設科舉時，初場試經義二道，《四書》義一道；

translations.literal: When examinations were first established, the first session tested two expositions on the classics and one on the Four Books;
translations.idiomatic: When the examinations were first instituted, the first session required two essays on the classics and one on the Four Books;

sentences.zh: 二場論一道；

translations.literal: the second session one discourse;
translations.idiomatic: the second session one discourse;

sentences.zh: 三場策一道。

translations.literal: the third session one policy question.
translations.idiomatic: and the third session one policy question.

sentences.zh: 中式後十日，復以騎、射、書、算、律五事試之。

translations.literal: Ten days after passing, they were again tested in the five matters of horsemanship, archery, calligraphy, calculation, and law.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after passing, candidates were tested again in horsemanship, archery, calligraphy, calculation, and law.

sentences.zh: 後頒科舉定式，初場試《四書》義三道，經義四道。

translations.literal: Later the fixed form for examinations was promulgated: the first session tested three Four Books expositions and four classical expositions.
translations.idiomatic: Later the standard examination format was issued: the first session required three Four Books essays and four classical essays.

sentences.zh: 《四書》主硃子《集註》，《易》主程《傳》、硃子《本義》，《書》主蔡氏傳及古註疏，《詩》主硃子《集傳》，《春秋》主左氏、公羊、穀梁三傳及胡安國、張洽傳，《禮記》主古註疏。

translations.literal: The Four Books followed Zhu Xi's Collected Commentaries; the Changes followed Cheng Yi's Commentary and Zhu Xi's Original Meaning; the Documents followed Cai Shen's commentary and ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; the Odes followed Zhu Xi's Collected Commentaries; the Spring and Autumn followed the three commentaries of Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang and the commentaries of Hu Anguo and Zhang Qia; the Record of Rites followed ancient commentaries and subcommentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were examined on Zhu Xi's commentaries for the Four Books; on Cheng Yi's and Zhu Xi's texts for the Changes; on Cai Shen and the ancient commentaries for the Documents; on Zhu Xi for the Odes; on the Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang traditions plus Hu Anguo and Zhang Qia for the Spring and Autumn; and on the ancient commentaries for the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，頒《四書五經大全》，廢註疏不用。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, the Great Compendium of the Four Books and Five Classics was issued, and commentaries and subcommentaries were abolished and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongle emperor the Great Compendium of the Four Books and Five Classics was promulgated, and the older commentaries were set aside.

sentences.zh: 其後，《春秋》亦不用張洽傳，禮記止用陳澔《集說》。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Spring and Autumn also no longer used Zhang Qia's commentary, and the Record of Rites used only Chen Hao's Collected Explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Qia's Spring and Autumn commentary was dropped as well, and only Chen Hao's Collected Explanations were used for the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二場試論一道，判五道，詔、誥、表、內科一道。

translations.literal: The second session tested one discourse, five legal judgments, and one each from the genres of edict, patent of enfeoffment, memorial to the throne, and inner-department document.
translations.idiomatic: The second session required one discourse, five legal judgments, and one document each in the forms of edict, enfeoffment patent, memorial, and inner-department dispatch.

sentences.zh: 三場試經史時務策五道。

translations.literal: The third session tested five policy questions on the classics, history, and current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The third session set five policy questions on the classics, history, and current affairs.

sentences.zh: 廷試，以三月朔。

translations.literal: The palace examination was on the first day of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination was held on the first day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 鄉試，直隸於京府，各省於布政司。

translations.literal: The provincial examination in the metropolitan area was under the capital prefecture; in each province it was under the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examinations in the capital region were run by the capital prefecture; in the provinces, by the provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 會試，於禮部。

translations.literal: The metropolitan examination was at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan examination was conducted by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 主考，鄉、會試俱二人。

translations.literal: Chief examiners: for both provincial and metropolitan examinations, two men.
translations.idiomatic: Each provincial and metropolitan examination had two chief examiners.

sentences.zh: 同考，鄉試四人，會試八人。

translations.literal: Associate examiners: four for the provincial examination, eight for the metropolitan.
translations.idiomatic: Associate examiners numbered four for the provincial examination and eight for the metropolitan.

sentences.zh: 提調一人，在內京官，在外布政司官。

translations.literal: One superintendent: inside the capital a capital official, outside a provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: One superintendent oversaw each examination—a capital official in the metropolitan region, a provincial administration commissioner in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 會試，禮部官監試二人，在內御史，在外按察司官。

translations.literal: For the metropolitan examination, two Ministry of Rites officials supervised the examination; inside the capital censors, outside surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan examination two Ministry of Rites officials supervised the sessions; in the capital censors served, in the provinces surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 會試，御史供給收掌試卷；

translations.literal: At the metropolitan examination, censors supplied and received the examination papers;
translations.idiomatic: At the metropolitan examination censors handled the supply and custody of papers;

sentences.zh: 彌封、謄錄、對讀、受卷及巡綽監門，搜檢懷挾，俱有定員，各執其事。

translations.literal: sealing, copying, proofreading, receiving papers, and patrol officers guarding gates and searching for concealed materials—all had fixed numbers of personnel, each performing his duty.
translations.idiomatic: while sealing, copying, proofreading, collecting papers, gate patrol, and searches for hidden crib notes each had assigned staff who carried out their tasks.

sentences.zh: 舉子，則國子生及府、州、縣學生員之學成者，儒士之未仕者，官之未入流者，皆由有司申舉性資敦厚、文行可稱者應之。

translations.literal: Candidates were students of the National University and degree students of prefectural, subprefectural, and county schools who had completed their studies, scholars not yet in office, and officials not yet in the regular grades—all recommended by the relevant offices as men of solid character and commendable learning and conduct who might respond.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates included National University students and prefectural, subprefectural, and county students who had finished their course, scholars not yet in office, and officials not yet in the regular grades. Local authorities nominated men of sound character and proven learning and conduct to sit the examinations.

sentences.zh: 其學校訓導專教生徒，及罷閑官吏，倡優之家，與居父母喪者，俱不許入試。

translations.literal: School instructors whose sole duty was teaching students, dismissed and idle officials, families of actors and entertainers, and those in mourning for parents were all forbidden to enter the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: School instructors whose only duty was teaching pupils, dismissed or idle officials, families of actors and entertainers, and those in mourning for a parent were barred from the examinations.

sentences.zh: 試卷之首，書三代姓名及其籍貫年甲，所習本經，所司印記。

translations.literal: At the head of the examination paper were written the candidate's name for three generations, native place, age, the classic he had studied as his specialty, and the seal of the office responsible.
translations.idiomatic: Each paper's cover sheet listed the candidate's name for three generations, native place, age, the classic he specialized in, and the seal of the sponsoring office.

sentences.zh: 試日入場，講問、代冒者有禁。

translations.literal: On the day of the examination, upon entering the grounds, explanation, questioning, and substitution were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On examination day, once candidates entered the compound, coaching, questioning, and impersonation were prohibited.

sentences.zh: 晚未納卷，給燭三枝。

translations.literal: If papers were not submitted by evening, three candles were provided.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had not handed in their papers by evening were allowed three candles' worth of light.

sentences.zh: 文字中迴避御名、廟號，及不許自序門第。

translations.literal: In the text one avoided the imperial name and temple names, and self-description of family status was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Essays had to avoid the emperor's personal name and temple names, and candidates could not describe their own family standing.

sentences.zh: 彌封編號作三合字。

translations.literal: Sealed registration numbers were made as three-part characters.
translations.idiomatic: Sealed registration numbers were written as three-part compound characters.

sentences.zh: 考試者用墨，謂之墨卷。

translations.literal: Examinees used black ink; these were called black papers.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates wrote in black ink—these were called black papers (mojuan).

sentences.zh: 謄錄用硃，謂之硃卷。

translations.literal: Copyists used vermilion; these were called vermilion papers.
translations.idiomatic: Copyists used vermilion ink—these were called vermilion papers (zhujuan).

sentences.zh: 試士之所，謂之貢院。

translations.literal: The place where scholars were examined was called the tribute court.
translations.idiomatic: The examination compound was called the tribute court (gongyuan).

sentences.zh: 諸生席舍，謂之號房。

translations.literal: The booths where students sat were called numbered rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Each candidate's booth was called a numbered cell (haofang).

sentences.zh: 人一軍守之，謂之號軍。

translations.literal: One soldier guarded each; these were called cell guards.
translations.idiomatic: One soldier guarded each booth—these were the cell guards (haojun).

sentences.zh: 試官入院，輒封鑰內外門戶。

translations.literal: When examination officials entered the compound, inner and outer gates were at once sealed and locked.
translations.idiomatic: Once the examiners entered, inner and outer gates were sealed.

sentences.zh: 在外提調、監試等謂之外簾官，在內主考、同考謂之內簾官。

translations.literal: Outside, the superintendent, supervisors, and the like were called outer-curtain officials; inside, chief and associate examiners were called inner-curtain officials.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendents and supervisors outside the sealed compound were outer-curtain officials; chief and associate examiners inside were inner-curtain officials.

sentences.zh: 廷試用翰林及朝臣文學之優者，為讀卷官。

translations.literal: For the palace examination, Hanlin academicians and court officials outstanding in letters served as reading officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination the finest literary minds among the Hanlin Academy and the court served as reading officials.

sentences.zh: 共閱對策，擬定名次，候臨軒。

translations.literal: Together they reviewed the policy answers, drafted the order of ranks, and awaited the imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: They read the policy answers together, drafted the ranking, and waited for the emperor's audience.

sentences.zh: 或如所擬，或有所更定，傳制唱第。

translations.literal: Sometimes it followed their draft, sometimes it was altered; the decree was transmitted and ranks were announced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor might accept their draft or revise it; then the decree was read and ranks announced.

sentences.zh: 狀元授修撰，榜眼、探花授編修，二、三甲考選庶起士者，皆為翰林官。

translations.literal: The Top Graduate was appointed Compiler, the Second and Third Graduates Editors; those selected through examination from the second and third cohorts as expectant scholars all became Hanlin officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Top Graduate was made a Compiler, the Second and Third Graduates Editors; expectant scholars chosen from the second and third cohorts all entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 其他或授給事、御史、主事、中書、行人、評事、太常、國子博士，或授府推官、知州、知縣等官。

translations.literal: Others might be appointed as supervising secretaries, censors, section chiefs, secretaries, messengers, reviewers, officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, or National University lecturers, or as prefectural judges, prefects, magistrates, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Others received posts as supervising secretaries, censors, section chiefs, secretaries, messengers, reviewers, Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials, National University lecturers, or as prefectural judges, prefects, and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 舉人、貢生不第、入監而選者，或授小京職，或授府佐及州縣正官，或授教職。

translations.literal: Presented Scholars and tribute students who failed to pass, entered the Directorate and were selected, might receive minor capital posts, prefectural assistants and regular prefectural and county posts, or teaching posts.
translations.idiomatic: Presented Scholars and tribute students who failed the metropolitan examination but entered the Directorate for selection might receive minor capital posts, prefectural assistantships, prefectural or county magistracies, or teaching appointments.

sentences.zh: 此明一代取士之大略也。

translations.literal: This is the broad outline of how the Ming dynasty recruited scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the Ming dynasty's broad system for recruiting talent through the examinations.

sentences.zh: 終明之世，右文左武。

translations.literal: Throughout the Ming, the civil was valued above the military.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Ming, civil learning held precedence over martial service.

sentences.zh: 然亦嘗設武科以收之，可得而附列也。

translations.literal: Yet a military examination track was also established at times to gather such men, which may be appended in a list.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dynasty also established a military examination track to recruit such men, which is recorded in the appendix below.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖起事，首羅賢才。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the founding emperor rose in arms, he first gathered worthy talent.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor first raised his banner, gathering able men was his first concern.

sentences.zh: 吳元年設文武二科取士之令，使有司勸諭民間秀士及智勇之人，以時勉學，俟開舉之歲，充貢京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu he issued an order establishing civil and military examinations to recruit scholars, directing the offices to encourage outstanding men of the people and men of wisdom and courage to study in season, so that when the year of opening examinations came they might present tribute at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu reign he ordered civil and military examinations, directing local authorities to encourage promising commoners and men of talent and courage to study steadily so that when examinations opened they could present themselves at the capital.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，詔曰：「漢、唐及宋，取士各有定制，然但貴文學而不求德藝之全。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu an edict said: "Han, Tang, and Song each had fixed regulations for recruiting scholars, yet they valued only literary learning and did not seek completeness of virtue and accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 an edict declared: "Han, Tang, and Song each had their own rules for recruiting officials, yet they prized literary skill alone and did not demand full virtue and practical ability.

sentences.zh: 前元待士甚優，而權豪勢要，每納奔競之人，夤緣阿附，輒竊仕祿。

translations.literal: The previous Yuan treated scholars very generously, yet the powerful and influential constantly admitted men who rushed to compete, who climbed by connections and flattery, and who then stole office and salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan treated scholars generously, but the powerful constantly admitted sycophants who bought their way in through connections and seized office and salary.

sentences.zh: 其懷材抱道者，恥與並進，甘隱山林而不出。

translations.literal: Those who harbored talent and embraced the Way were ashamed to advance alongside them and willingly hid in mountains and forests without coming forth.
translations.idiomatic: Men of real talent and principle were ashamed to advance beside them and chose to remain in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 風俗之弊，一至於此。

translations.literal: The corruption of custom had reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Custom had decayed to that extent.

sentences.zh: 自今年八月始，特設科舉，務取經明行修、博通古今、名實相稱者。

translations.literal: Beginning this year in the eighth month, examinations are specially established, aiming to take men clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, broadly versed in past and present, whose reputation and reality match.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning this eighth month I establish examinations to select men who are masters of the classics and upright in conduct, broadly learned in past and present, and whose reputation matches their substance.

sentences.zh: 朕將親策於廷，第其高下而任之以官。

translations.literal: I shall personally examine them in court, rank them high and low, and appoint them to office.
translations.idiomatic: I shall question them myself in court, rank them, and appoint them to office accordingly.

sentences.zh: 使中外文臣皆由科舉而進，非科舉者毋得與官。」

translations.literal: Let civil officials within and without all advance through examinations; those not from examinations shall not receive office."
translations.idiomatic: All civil officials at court and in the provinces shall rise through the examinations; no one who has not passed them shall hold office."

sentences.zh: 於是京師行省各舉鄉試：直隸貢額百人，河南、山東、山西、陝西、北平、福建、江西、浙江、湖廣皆四十人，廣西、廣東皆二十五人，纔多或不及者，不拘額數。

translations.literal: Thereupon the capital and each province held provincial examinations: the metropolitan area had a quota of one hundred, Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Beiping, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Huguang each forty, Guangxi and Guangdong each twenty-five; where talent was more or less, quotas were not rigidly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial examinations were then held in the capital and in each province: the metropolitan region was allotted one hundred places; Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Beiping, Fujian, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Huguang forty each; Guangxi and Guangdong twenty-five each. Where talent exceeded or fell short of the quota, the numbers were not held rigid.

sentences.zh: 高麗、安南、占城，詔許其國士子於本國鄉試，貢赴京師。

translations.literal: For Korea, Annam, and Champa, an edict permitted their country's scholars to take the provincial examination in their own country and present tribute to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Korea, Annam, and Champa were permitted to hold provincial examinations at home and send their graduates to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年會試，取中一百二十名。

translations.literal: The next year at the metropolitan examination one hundred twenty passed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the metropolitan examination passed one hundred twenty candidates.

sentences.zh: 帝親制策問，試於奉天殿，擢吳伯宗第一。

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed the policy questions and examined them in the Hall of Complying with Heaven, elevating Wu Bozong to first place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed the policy questions himself and examined candidates in the Hall of Complying with Heaven, placing Wu Bozong first.

sentences.zh: 午門外張掛黃榜，奉天殿宣諭，賜宴中書省。

translations.literal: Outside the Meridian Gate a yellow placard was posted; in the Hall of Complying with Heaven the decree was proclaimed; a banquet was granted at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow placard was posted outside the Meridian Gate; the results were proclaimed in the Hall of Complying with Heaven; and a banquet was given at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 授伯宗為禮部員外郎，餘以次授官有差。

translations.literal: Bozong was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; the rest received offices in descending order with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong was appointed vice minister of rites; the others received offices in rank order.

sentences.zh: 時以天下初定，令各行省連試三年，且以官多缺員，舉人俱免會試，赴京聽選。

translations.literal: At the time, because the realm had just been settled, each province was ordered to hold examinations for three consecutive years, and because many offices lacked incumbents, Presented Scholars were all exempted from the metropolitan examination and went to the capital to await selection.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm had only just been pacified, each province was ordered to hold examinations for three years running; with so many vacant posts, Presented Scholars were exempted from the metropolitan examination and sent to the capital for appointment.

sentences.zh: 又擢其年少俊異者張唯、王輝等為翰林院編修，蕭韶為祕書監直長，令入禁中文華堂肄業，太子贊善大夫宋濂等為之師。

translations.literal: He also elevated the young and outstanding Zhang Wei, Wang Hui, and others as Hanlin editors, Xiao Shao as director of the Palace Secretariat, ordering them to study in the Wenhua Hall within the Forbidden City, with the crown prince's tutor Song Lian and others as their teachers.
translations.idiomatic: He also selected promising young men such as Zhang Wei and Wang Hui as Hanlin editors, made Xiao Shao a director of the Palace Secretariat, and had them study in the Wenhua Hall inside the Forbidden City under Song Lian and other tutors to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝聽政之暇，輒幸堂中，評其文字優劣，日給光祿酒饌。

translations.literal: In his leisure from hearing government, the emperor would visit the hall, appraise the quality of their writing, and daily supply wine and food from the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals from governing, the emperor visited the hall, judged their writing, and daily supplied wine and food from the Imperial Household Service.

sentences.zh: 每食，皇太子、親王迭為之主，賜白金、弓矢、鞍馬及冬夏衣，寵遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: At each meal the crown prince and imperial princes took turns as hosts; white gold, bows and arrows, saddles and horses, and winter and summer clothing were bestowed; favor toward them was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: At each meal the crown prince and imperial princes took turns as hosts. They received gifts of silver, bows and arrows, saddles and horses, and seasonal clothing—favor rarely shown so lavishly.

sentences.zh: 既而謂所取多後生少年，能以所學措諸行事者寡，乃但令有司察舉賢才，而罷科舉不用。

translations.literal: Before long he said that those taken were mostly young men in their prime, and few could apply what they had learned to action; he therefore ordered only that the offices investigate and recommend worthy talent, and abolished examinations without using them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he concluded that most of those selected were young men who could rarely put their learning into practice. He ordered local authorities to investigate and recommend talent instead, and suspended the examinations.

sentences.zh: 至十五年，復設。

translations.literal: By the fifteenth year they were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen they were restored.

sentences.zh: 十七年始定科舉之式，命禮部頒行各省，後遂以為永制，而薦舉漸輕，久且廢不用矣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the form of examinations was first fixed; the Ministry of Rites was ordered to promulgate it to each province; later it became the permanent system, while recommendation grew lighter and in time was abandoned and not used.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen the examination format was fixed and promulgated to every province, becoming the permanent system. Recommendation gradually lost weight and was eventually abandoned.

sentences.zh: 十八年廷試，擢一甲進士丁顯等為翰林院修撰，二甲馬京等為編修，吳文為檢討。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year at the palace examination, first-cohort jinshi Ding Xian and others were elevated to Hanlin compilers, second-cohort Ma Jing and others to editors, and Wu Wen to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination in year eighteen, first-cohort jinshi such as Ding Xian were made Hanlin compilers, second-cohort graduates such as Ma Jing were made editors, and Wu Wen was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 進士之入翰林，自此始也。

translations.literal: Jinshi entering the Hanlin began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: From this point jinshi regularly entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 使進士觀政於諸司，其在翰林、承敕監等衙門者，曰庶起士。

translations.literal: Jinshi were made to observe government in the various offices; those in the Hanlin, Imperial Patent Office, and similar yamens were called expectant scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi were sent to observe government in the various offices; those posted to the Hanlin Academy, Imperial Patent Office, and similar agencies were called expectant scholars (shujishi).

sentences.zh: 進士之為庶起士，亦自此始也。

translations.literal: Jinshi serving as expectant scholars also began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: The post of jinshi as expectant Hanlin scholar also dates from this time.

sentences.zh: 其在六部、都察院、通政司、大理寺等衙門者仍稱進士，觀政進士之名亦自此始也。

translations.literal: Those in the Six Ministries, Censorate, Office of Transmission, Court of Revision, and similar yamens were still called jinshi; the name "jinshi observing government" also began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Those assigned to the Six Ministries, Censorate, Office of Transmission, Court of Revision, and similar agencies retained the title jinshi—the term "jinshi observing government" also begins here.

sentences.zh: 其後試額有增減，條例有變更，考官有內外輕重，闈事有是非得失。

translations.literal: Thereafter examination quotas increased or decreased, regulations changed, examiners had differences of weight between inner and outer roles, and examination affairs had rights and wrongs, gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter quotas rose and fell, regulations changed, the weight of inner and outer examiners shifted, and examination affairs produced controversies, successes, and failures.

sentences.zh: 其細者勿論，其有關於國是者不可無述也。

translations.literal: Minor matters need not be discussed; those bearing on the fundamental affairs of state cannot go unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Minor details may be passed over, but matters bearing on the fundamental affairs of state must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 鄉試之額，洪武十七年詔不拘額數，從實充貢。

translations.literal: For provincial examination quotas, in Hongwu year seventeen an edict said quotas were not fixed; tribute was filled according to actual talent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 17 an edict declared that provincial quotas were not fixed—each province was to send as many qualified candidates as it actually had.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年始有定額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi fixed quotas first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed quotas were first set in the first year of the Hongxi reign.

sentences.zh: 其後漸增。

translations.literal: Thereafter they gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: They rose gradually thereafter.

sentences.zh: 至正統間，南北直隸定以百名，江西六十五名，他省又自五而殺，至雲南二十名為最少。

translations.literal: By the Zhengtong period, the two metropolitan regions were fixed at one hundred each, Jiangxi at sixty-five, other provinces decreasing by fives down to Yunnan's twenty as the least.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhengtong reign the two metropolitan regions were fixed at one hundred each, Jiangxi at sixty-five, and other provinces stepped down by fives to a minimum of twenty in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，增至四十，而貴州亦二十名。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period they increased to forty, and Guizhou also had twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing some provinces rose to forty, and Guizhou was also allotted twenty.

sentences.zh: 慶、曆、啟、禎間，兩直隸益增至一百三十餘名，他省漸增，無出百名者。

translations.literal: Between the Qingli, Wanli, Tianqi, and Chongzhen reigns the two metropolitan regions further increased to more than one hundred thirty each; other provinces gradually increased, none exceeding one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: From the Longqing through Chongzhen reigns the two metropolitan regions rose to more than one hundred thirty each; other provinces grew as well, though none exceeded one hundred.

sentences.zh: 交阯初開以十名為額，迨棄其地乃止。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi was first opened, ten places were allotted; when that territory was abandoned it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi was first incorporated it was allotted ten places; the quota ended when the territory was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 會試之額，國初無定，少至三十二人，其多者，若洪武乙丑、永樂丙戌，至四百七十二人。

translations.literal: Metropolitan examination quotas at the dynasty's beginning were not fixed, falling as low as thirty-two; at their height, as in Hongwu yichou and Yongle bingxu, they reached four hundred seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Early metropolitan quotas were not fixed, falling as low as thirty-two and rising as high as four hundred seventy-two, as in the Hongwu yichou and Yongle bingxu cycles.

sentences.zh: 其後或百名，或二百名，或二百五十名，或三百五十名，增損不一，皆臨期奏請定奪。

translations.literal: Thereafter sometimes one hundred, sometimes two hundred, two hundred fifty, or three hundred fifty—increases and decreases were not uniform; all were decided by memorial on the eve of the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Later quotas varied—one hundred, two hundred, two hundred fifty, or three hundred fifty—each decided by memorial just before the examination.

sentences.zh: 至成化乙未而後，率取三百名，有因題請及恩詔而廣五十名或百名者，非恆制也。

translations.literal: From Chenghua yiwei onward the rate was three hundred; when fifty or one hundred extra were granted on special request or by grace edict, this was not the regular system.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chenghua yiwei cycle onward the standard quota was three hundred; additions of fifty or one hundred on special petition or by grace edict were exceptions.

sentences.zh: 初制，禮闈取士，不分南北。

translations.literal: Under the initial system, the Ministry of Rites examination recruited scholars without distinguishing north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Under the original system the metropolitan examination at the Ministry of Rites did not distinguish northern and southern candidates.

sentences.zh: 自洪武丁丑，考官劉三吾、白信蹈所取宋琮等五十二人，皆南士。

translations.literal: From Hongwu dingchou, the examiners Liu Sanwu and Bai Xindao took Song Cong and fifty-one others—all were southern scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu dingchou cycle the examiners Liu Sanwu and Bai Xindao passed Song Cong and fifty-one others—all southerners.

sentences.zh: 三月，廷試，擢陳䢿為第一。

translations.literal: In the third month at the palace examination Chen Anhe was elevated to first place.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination in the third month Chen Anhe was placed first.

sentences.zh: 帝怒所取之偏，命侍讀張信等十二人覆閱，䢿亦與焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that the selection was biased and ordered the reader-in-waiting Zhang Xin and eleven others to review again; Anhe was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered by the bias, ordered twelve readers including Zhang Xin to re-examine the papers; Anhe was among those reviewed again.

sentences.zh: 帝猶怒不已，悉誅信蹈及信、䢿等，戍三吾於邊，親自閱卷，取任伯安等六十一人。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger still did not cease; he executed all of Xindao, Xin, Anhe, and the rest, exiled Sanwu to the frontier, personally reviewed the papers, and took Ren Bo'an and sixty others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath would not subside: he executed Bai Xindao, Zhang Xin, Chen Anhe, and the others involved, banished Liu Sanwu to the borderlands, personally re-read the papers, and passed sixty-one men including Ren Bo'an.

sentences.zh: 六月復廷試，以韓克忠為第一。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the palace examination was held again, with Han Kezhong as first.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the palace examination was repeated, with Han Kezhong placed first.

sentences.zh: 皆北士也。

translations.literal: All were northerners.
translations.idiomatic: All were northerners.

sentences.zh: 然訖永樂間，未嘗分地而取。

translations.literal: Yet through the Yongle period, they never selected by region.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the Yongle reign the examinations never again allotted places by region.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，仁宗命楊士奇等定取士之額，南人十六，北人十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, Emperor Renzong ordered Yang Shiqi and others to fix the quota for selecting scholars—sixteen southerners, fourteen northerners.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 (1425) Emperor Renzong had Yang Shiqi and his colleagues set the recruitment quota at sixteen southerners and fourteen northerners.

sentences.zh: 宣德、正統間，分為南、北、中卷，以百人為率，則南取五十五名，北取三十五名，中取十名。

translations.literal: In the Xuande and Zhengtong periods they were divided into southern, northern, and central rolls; taking one hundred as the standard, the south took fifty-five, the north thirty-five, the center ten.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande and Zhengtong the papers were split into southern, northern, and central rolls; on a quota of one hundred, fifty-five went to the south, thirty-five to the north, and ten to the center.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，詔書遵永樂間例。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai an edict followed the Yongle precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign an edict revived the Yongle practice.

sentences.zh: 二年辛未，禮部方奉行，而給事中李侃爭之，言：「部臣欲專以文詞，多取南人。」

translations.literal: In the second year, xinwei, the Ministry of Rites was just implementing it when supervising secretary Li Kan disputed it, saying: "The ministry intends to rely solely on literary polish and take more southerners."
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 2 (1452), as the Ministry of Rites was putting the rule into effect, supervising secretary Li Kan objected: "The ministry wishes to judge solely by literary polish and pass more southerners."

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎羅綺亦助侃言。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments Luo Qi also aided Kan's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Punishments Luo Qi backed Kan's petition.

sentences.zh: 事下禮部，覆奏：「臣等奉詔書，非私請也。」

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Ministry of Rites, which memorialized in reply: "Your servants received the imperial edict; this is no private request."
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Ministry of Rites, which replied: "We are acting on the edict, not pressing a private interest."

sentences.zh: 景帝命遵詔書，不從侃議。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing ordered compliance with the edict and did not follow Kan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingtai Emperor upheld the edict and rejected Kan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，給事中徐廷章復請依正統間例。

translations.literal: Before long, supervising secretary Xu Tingzhang again requested following the Zhengtong precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, supervising secretary Xu Tingzhang again asked that the Zhengtong quotas be restored.

sentences.zh: 五年甲戌，會試，禮部奏請裁定，於是復從廷章言，分南、北、中卷：南卷，應天及蘇、鬆諸府，浙江、江西、福建、湖廣、廣東；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, jiaxu, at the metropolitan examination the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting a ruling; then they again followed Tingzhang's words and divided southern, northern, and central rolls: the southern roll—Nanjing and the prefectures of Suzhou and Song, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Huguang, Guangdong;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 5 (1454), when the metropolitan examination came, the ministry sought imperial confirmation and again adopted Tingzhang's scheme, dividing southern, northern, and central rolls. The southern roll comprised Nanjing; Suzhou and Song; Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Huguang, and Guangdong;

sentences.zh: 北卷，順天、山東、山西、河南、陝西；

translations.literal: the northern roll—Shuntian, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi;
translations.idiomatic: the northern roll comprised Shuntian, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, and Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 中卷，四川、廣西、雲南、貴州及鳳陽、廬州二府，滁、徐、和三州也。

translations.literal: the central roll—Sichuan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, and the two prefectures of Fengyang and Luzhou, and the three subprefectures of Chuzhou, Xuzhou, and Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: the central roll comprised Sichuan, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fengyang and Luzhou, and the subprefectures of Chuzhou, Xuzhou, and Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 成化二十二年，萬安當國，周洪謨為禮部尚書，皆四川人，乃因布政使潘稹之請，南北各減二名，以益於中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Chenghua, when Wan An held the state, Zhou Hongmo was Minister of Rites—both were Sichuan men—and on the request of provincial administration commissioner Pan Ji they reduced two places each from north and south to add to the center.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 22 (1486), with Wan An dominant at court and Zhou Hongmo—both Sichuan natives—as Minister of Rites, Pan Ji's request from the provincial administration led to two quota seats being cut from north and south alike and reassigned to the central roll.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，復從舊制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi the old system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 2 (1489) saw a return to the earlier quotas.

sentences.zh: 嗣後相沿不改。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was carried on unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement then remained unchanged for generations.

sentences.zh: 惟正德三年，給事中趙鐸承劉瑾指，請廣河南、陝西、山東、西鄉試之額。

translations.literal: Only in the third year of Zhengde, on instructions from Liu Jin conveyed by supervising secretary Zhao Duo, was a request made to expand the provincial examination quotas for Henan, Shaanxi, Shandong, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Zhengde 3 (1508), when supervising secretary Zhao Duo acted at Liu Jin's direction, were the provincial quotas raised for Henan, Shaanxi, Shandong, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 乃增陝西為百，河南為九十五，山東、西俱九十。

translations.literal: Then Shaanxi was increased to one hundred, Henan to ninety-five, Shandong and Shaanxi both to ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi's quota was set at one hundred, Henan's at ninety-five, and Shandong and Shaanxi each at ninety.

sentences.zh: 而以會試分南、北、中卷為不均，乃增四川額十名，併入南卷，其餘併入北卷，南北均取一百五十名。

translations.literal: Because dividing the metropolitan examination into southern, northern, and central rolls was deemed uneven, ten places were added to Sichuan and merged into the southern roll; the remainder were merged into the northern roll, and north and south each took one hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the three-roll metropolitan split unfair, ten seats were added to Sichuan and folded into the southern roll, the rest into the northern, and north and south were each fixed at one hundred fifty passes.

sentences.zh: 蓋瑾陝西人，而閣臣焦芳河南人，票旨相附和，各徇其私。

translations.literal: Jin was a Shaanxi man, while Grand Secretary Jiao Fang was a Henan man; their jointly drafted rescripts supported each other, each indulging his own interest.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was native to Shaanxi and Grand Secretary Jiao Fang to Henan; their memorial drafts reinforced one another, each man serving his own province.

sentences.zh: 瑾、芳敗，旋復其舊。

translations.literal: When Jin and Fang fell, the old quotas were swiftly restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin and Fang fell from power the earlier quotas were promptly restored.

sentences.zh: 初制，兩京鄉試，主考皆用翰林。

translations.literal: Under the initial system, for the provincial examinations of the two capitals the chief examiners were all drawn from the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the metropolitan-area provincial examinations at both capitals were presided over exclusively by Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 而各省考官，先期於儒官、儒士內聘明經公正者為之，故有不在朝列累秉文衡者。

translations.literal: For the provincial examiners of each province, beforehand from among Confucian officials and scholars they engaged those versed in the classics who were upright, hence there were those not in the court ranks who repeatedly held the literary balance.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial associate examiners were recruited in advance from among local scholar-officials known for classical learning and integrity, so that men outside the central bureaucracy sometimes held the testing brush repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，令布、按二司同巡按御史，推舉見任教官年五十以下、三十以上、文學廉謹者，聘充考官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai an order directed the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners together with the touring censor to recommend incumbent instructors between fifty and thirty years of age who were learned, upright, and careful, and engage them as examiners.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 3 (1452) required regional commissioners and the touring censor to nominate active instructors aged thirty to fifty who were literate and upright, and appoint them as examiners.

sentences.zh: 於是教官主試，遂為定例。

translations.literal: Thereupon instructors as chief examiners became the fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: School instructors as chief examiners thus became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 其後有司徇私，聘取或非其人，監臨官又往往侵奪其職掌。

translations.literal: Later the local offices showed favoritism, engagements were sometimes not the right men, and the supervising officials often usurped their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Later local officials favored their own circles, unsuitable men were hired, and supervising commissioners often seized the examiners' authority.

sentences.zh: 成化十五年，御史許進請各省俱視兩京例，特命翰林主考。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua, censor Xu Jin requested that every province follow the two-capital precedent and specially appoint Hanlin as chief examiners.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 15 (1479) censor Xu Jin asked that every province follow the capital model and send Hanlin scholars as chief examiners.

sentences.zh: 帝諭禮部嚴飭私弊，而不從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the Ministry of Rites strictly to admonish against private abuses, but did not grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Ministry of Rites to crack down on corruption but declined Xu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 屢戒外簾官毋奪主考權，考官不當，則舉主連坐。

translations.literal: Again and again he warned outer-curtain officials not to seize the chief examiners' power; when examiners were unfit, the recommending official was implicated by joint penalty.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly forbade outer-curtain supervisors to override chief examiners and ruled that if an examiner proved unworthy, whoever had nominated him would share the punishment.

sentences.zh: 又令提學考定教官等第，以備聘取。

translations.literal: He also ordered the education intendant to rank instructors by grade for ready engagement.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered education intendants to grade instructors so suitable men could be chosen quickly.

sentences.zh: 然相沿既久，積習難移。

translations.literal: Yet the practice had long continued and accumulated habits were hard to shift.
translations.idiomatic: Custom had hardened over time, however, and old habits resisted reform.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年，掌國子監謝鐸言：「考官皆御史方面所辟召，職分即卑，聽其指使，以外簾官預定去取，名為防閑，實則關節，而科舉之法壞矣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, Xie Duo, chief of the Directorate of Education, said: "The examiners are all recruited by the censors and regional officials; their posts are low, and they obey directions; the outer-curtain officials pre-determine who passes and fails in the name of guarding against impropriety but in fact control the whole process, and the examination system is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 14 (1501) Xie Duo, superintendent of the Imperial Academy, reported: "Provincial examiners are hired by censors and regional commissioners; their rank is low and they take orders. Outer-curtain officials decide passes and failures in advance—nominally to prevent abuse, actually to run every lever—and the recruitment system is ruined.

sentences.zh: 乞敕兩京大臣，各舉部屬等官素有文望者，每省差二員主考，庶幾前弊可革。」

translations.literal: I beg that His Majesty order the senior ministers of the two capitals each to recommend subordinate officials of long literary standing, two per province to serve as chief examiners, so that the earlier abuses may be reformed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that ministers in both capitals nominate proven literary men from their staffs, two per province as chief examiners, so that these abuses can be ended."

sentences.zh: 時未能從。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not act on it at the time.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年，用兵部侍郎張璁言，各省主試皆遣京官或進士，每省二人馳往。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing, on the memorial of Vice Minister of War Zhang Cong, every province's chief examiners were to dispatch capital officials or jinshi, two per province riding out in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 7 (1528), following Vice Minister Zhang Cong, each province was to receive two capital officials or jinshi degree-holders as chief examiners dispatched from court.

sentences.zh: 初，兩京房考亦皆取教職，至是命各加科部官一員，閱兩科、兩京房考，復罷科部勿遣，而各省主考亦不遣京官。

translations.literal: At first the associate examiners for both capitals also all took school instructors; by this order each capital added one ministry official to review both capitals' associate examiners for two cycles; then ministry dispatch was stopped again, and capital officials were no longer sent as provincial chief examiners either.
translations.idiomatic: Initially both capitals' associate examiners had also been instructors; under the new rule each capital added one ministry examiner to oversee two cycles of provincial examining, then ministry appointments ceased again and provincial chief examiners were no longer sent from the capital.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆十一年，詔定科場事宜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli an edict fixed examination-hall procedures.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 11 (1583) brought an edict standardizing examination procedure.

sentences.zh: 部議復舉張璁之說，言：「彼時因主考與監臨官禮節小嫌，故行止二科而罷，今宜仍遣廷臣。」

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and again raised Zhang Cong's proposal, saying: "At that time because of minor etiquette friction between chief examiners and supervising officials it was tried for two cycles and stopped; now it is fitting again to dispatch court grandees."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry revived Zhang Cong's argument: "The earlier trial ended after two cycles because of ceremonial friction between chief examiners and supervisors; court examiners should again be sent."

sentences.zh: 由是浙江、江西、福建、湖廣皆用編修、檢討，他省用科部官，而同考亦多用甲科，教職僅取一二而已。

translations.literal: Hence Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, and Huguang all used compilers and proofreaders; other provinces used ministry officials, and associate examiners also mostly drew on jinshi men, with instructors taking only one or two places.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, and Huguang henceforth used Hanlin compilers and proofreaders; other provinces used ministry officials; associate examiners were largely jinshi scholars, with only one or two instructors retained.

sentences.zh: 蓋自嘉靖二十五年從給事中萬虞愷言，各省鄉試精聘教官，不足則聘外省推官、知縣以益之。

translations.literal: Generally from the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing, on supervising secretary Wan Yuqing's words, each province's provincial examination carefully engaged instructors, and when insufficient, engaged outer-province pushers of officials and magistrates to supplement them.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiajing 25 (1546), on Wan Yuqing's advice, provinces carefully hired instructors for the provincial exam and, when short, supplemented them with magistrates and judicial pushers from other circuits.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，又從南京御史奏，兩京同考用京官進士，《易》、《詩》、《書》各二人，《春秋》、《禮記》各一人，其餘乃參用教官。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, again on a Nanjing censor's memorial, both capitals' associate examiners used capital officials and jinshi—two each for the Changes, Odes, and Documents, one each for Spring and Autumn and the Rites—and only thereafter were instructors mixed in.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 43 (1564), after a Nanjing censor's memorial, both capitals used capital officials and jinshi as associates—two each for the Odes, Changes, and Documents, one each for Spring and Autumn and the Rites—with instructors filling out the roster.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年，復議兩京同考、教官衰老者遣回，北京取足於觀政進士、候補甲科，南京於附近知縣、推官取用。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wanli, it was again deliberated that aged instructor associates at both capitals be sent home; Beijing would make up its quota from observing-policy jinshi and jinshi on waiting lists, Nanjing from nearby magistrates and pushers.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 4 (1576) reconsidered the rule: elderly instructor-associates were sent home; Beijing filled gaps from jinshi awaiting assignment and from ranked substitutes, Nanjing from nearby magistrates and pushers.

sentences.zh: 至是教官益絀。

translations.literal: By then instructors were further diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Instructors' role was thereby reduced still further.

sentences.zh: 初制，會試同考八人，三人用翰林，五人用教職。

translations.literal: Under the initial system, metropolitan associate examiners were eight—three from Hanlin, five from instructors.
translations.idiomatic: Originally eight associate examiners served the metropolitan exam—three Hanlin, five instructors.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年，從禮部尚書胡濙請，俱用翰林、部曹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai, on Minister of Rites Hu Ying's request, all were drawn from Hanlin and ministry department staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 5 (1454), at Hu Ying's request, all associates came from Hanlin and ministry bureaus.

sentences.zh: 其後房考漸增。

translations.literal: Thereafter session examiners gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: Session examiners gradually increased thereafter.

sentences.zh: 至正德六年，命用十七人，翰林十一人，科部各三人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde an order used seventeen men—eleven Hanlin, three each from the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 6 (1511) fixed the roster at seventeen: eleven Hanlin, three from each relevant ministry.

sentences.zh: 分《詩經》房五，《易經》、《書經》各四，《春秋》、《禮記》各二。

translations.literal: Five for the Odes session, four each for the Changes and Documents sessions, two each for Spring and Autumn and the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Five examiners for the Odes, four each for Changes and Documents, two each for Spring and Autumn and the Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年，禮部尚書夏言論科場三事，其一言會試同考，例用講讀十一人，今講讀止十一人，當盡入場，方足供事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing, Minister of Rites Xia Yan discussed three matters of the examination field; one concerned metropolitan associates, customarily eleven lecturers and readers, but now lecturers and readers number only eleven—when all enter the hall they barely suffice for the tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 11 (1532) Xia Yan laid out three examination reforms. On metropolitan associates, custom called for eleven lecturers and readers-in-waiting, yet there were only eleven such posts in all—barely enough once every man entered the hall.

sentences.zh: 乞於部科再簡三四人，以補翰林不足之數。

translations.literal: I beg to select another three or four men from the ministries to supplement the Hanlin shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that three or four more ministry officials be picked to cover the Hanlin shortfall.

sentences.zh: 世宗命如所請。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor ordered as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 然偶一行之，輒如其舊。

translations.literal: Yet when occasionally carried out, it soon reverted to the old way.
translations.idiomatic: When the change was tried it was soon abandoned and the old practice restored.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年，以《易》卷多，減《書》之一以增於《易》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli, because the Changes papers were many, one was taken from Documents and added to Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 11, because the Changes cohort was large, one examiner was moved from Documents to Changes.

sentences.zh: 十四年，《書》卷復多，乃增翰林一人，以補《書》之缺。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Documents papers were many again, so one Hanlin was added to fill the Documents gap.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 14, with Documents again overloaded, one more Hanlin examiner was added for that session.

sentences.zh: 至四十四年，用給事中餘懋孳奏，《詩》、《易》各增一房，共為二十房，翰林十二人，科部各四人，至明末不變。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, on supervising secretary Yu Maozi's memorial, one session each was added for the Odes and Changes, making twenty sessions in all—twelve Hanlin, four each from the ministries—unchanged to the dynasty's end.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 44 (1616), on Yu Maozi's memorial, added one session each for Odes and Changes, for twenty sessions total—twelve Hanlin, four per ministry—a roster that held until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，賜諸進士宴於中書省。

translations.literal: In the early Hongwu period the throne bestowed banquets on all jinshi at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early Hongwu banquets for new jinshi were held at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，賜宴於中軍都督府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande banquets were bestowed at the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 5 (1430) moved the feast to the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 八年，賜宴於禮部，自是遂著為令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year banquets were bestowed at the Ministry of Rites; from this it was fixed as ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 8 (1433) fixed the venue at the Ministry of Rites, where it remained thereafter.

sentences.zh: 庶起士之選，自洪武乙丑擇進士為之，不專屬於翰林也。

translations.literal: Selection of expectant Hanlin scholars, from Hongwu yichou chose jinshi for it, not exclusively belonging to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant Hanlin scholars were first chosen from among new jinshi in Hongwu yichou (1385) and were not yet an exclusively Hanlin institution.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，既授一甲三人曾棨、周述、周孟簡等官，復命於第二甲擇文學優等楊相等五十人，及善書者湯流等十人，俱為翰林院庶起士，庶起士遂專屬翰林矣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle, after the three men of the first rank Zeng Qi, Zhou Shu, Zhou Mengjian and others had been appointed to office, he again ordered from the second rank fifty men of superior literary attainment such as Yang Xiang, and ten skilled at calligraphy such as Tang Liu, all made expectant Hanlin scholars of the Hanlin Academy; expectant Hanlin scholars then came to belong exclusively to the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 2 (1404) assigned the three top graduates—Zeng Qi, Zhou Shu, and Zhou Mengjian—then took fifty especially gifted second-rank men including Yang Xiang and ten skilled calligraphers including Tang Liu as expectant Hanlin scholars, at which point the post became a purely Hanlin preserve.

sentences.zh: 復命學士解縉等選才資英敏者，就學文淵閣。

translations.literal: Again he ordered academician Xie Jin and others to select men of keen talent to study at the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Academician Xie Jin and others pick the brightest men for study in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 縉等選修撰棨，編修述、孟簡，庶起士相等共二十八人，以應二十八宿之數。

translations.literal: Jin and others selected compiler Qi, editors Shu and Mengjian, expectant scholars Xiang and others totaling twenty-eight men, to match the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
translations.idiomatic: They chose Compiler Zeng Qi, Editors Zhou Shu and Zhou Mengjian, Expectant Scholar Yang Xiang, and twenty-five others—twenty-eight in all—to correspond to the Twenty-eight Mansions.

sentences.zh: 庶起士周忱自陳少年願學。

translations.literal: Expectant scholar Zhou Chen voluntarily stated that in his youth he wished to study.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant Scholar Zhou Chen petitioned that, being young, he wished to continue his training.

sentences.zh: 帝喜而俞之，增忱為二十九人。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and approved it, increasing Chen to make twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly assented and added Chen, bringing the cohort to twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 司禮監月給筆墨紙，光祿給朝暮饌，禮部月給膏燭鈔，人三錠，工部擇近第宅居之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonies monthly supplied brush, ink, and paper; the Court of Imperial Entertainments supplied morning and evening meals; the Ministry of Rites monthly supplied candles and lamp-oil money, three ingots per man; the Ministry of Works chose residences near the academy for their dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonies issued monthly stationery; the Court of Imperial Entertainments fed them morning and night; the Ministry of Rites allotted three ingots of candle and lamp money per man each month; the Ministry of Works lodged them in houses near the academy.

sentences.zh: 帝時至館召試。

translations.literal: The emperor from time to time came to the academy to summon them for tests.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the academy intermittently to test them.

sentences.zh: 五日一休沐，必使內臣隨行，且給校尉騶從。

translations.literal: Every five days one rest day; they had to be accompanied by inner eunuchs, and were also given guard cavaliers as escort.
translations.idiomatic: They rested every fifth day but had to be escorted on leave by palace eunuchs and were given guard cavalry as retinue.

sentences.zh: 是年所選王英、王直、段民、周忱、陳敬宗、李時勉等，名傳後世者，不下十餘人。

translations.literal: Among those selected that year—Wang Ying, Wang Zhi, Duan Min, Zhou Chen, Chen Jingzong, Li Shimian, and others—those whose names have been handed down to later generations were not fewer than ten.
translations.idiomatic: That year's cohort—Wang Ying, Wang Zhi, Duan Min, Zhou Chen, Chen Jingzong, Li Shimian, and others—included more than ten men whose reputations outlived the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其後每科所選，多寡無定額。

translations.literal: Thereafter the number selected each cycle was large or small with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Later cohorts varied in size with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年乙未選六十二人，而宣德二年丁未止邢恭一人，以其在翰林院習四夷譯書久，他人俱不得與也。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle, yiwei, sixty-two were selected; in the second year of Xuande, dingwei, only Xing Gong alone—because he had long studied the four barbarian scripts of translation in the Hanlin Academy, the others all could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 13 (1415) chose sixty-two men; Xuande 2 (1427) chose only Xing Gong, who alone had long trained in foreign translation at the Hanlin Academy while the rest were passed over.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，給事中塗旦以累科不選庶起士，請循祖制行之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, supervising secretary Tu Dan, because for successive cycles expectant Hanlin scholars had not been selected, requested that the ancestral system be followed and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 4 (1491) supervising secretary Tu Dan, noting several cycles without new expectant scholars, asked that the ancestral practice be restored.

sentences.zh: 大學士徐溥言：「自永樂二年以來，或間科一選，或連科屢選，或數科不選，或合三科同選，初無定限。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Pu said: "From the second year of Yongle onward, sometimes one cycle was selected, sometimes several cycles in succession, sometimes several cycles without selection, sometimes three cycles selected together—at first there was no fixed limit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xu Pu replied: "Since Yongle 2 selection has been irregular—sometimes one cycle, sometimes several in a row, sometimes none for years, sometimes three cycles at once—with no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 或內閣自選，或禮部選送，或會禮部同選，或限年歲，或拘地方，或採譽望，或就廷試卷中查取，或別出題考試，亦無定制。

translations.literal: Sometimes the inner cabinet chose, sometimes the Ministry of Rites sent nominations, sometimes the ministries chose together, sometimes age was limited, sometimes region was constrained, sometimes reputation was sought, sometimes taken from palace examination papers, sometimes tested by separate topics—likewise there was no fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the inner cabinet picked men, sometimes the Ministry of Rites forwarded names, sometimes ministries chose jointly; sometimes age or region was imposed, sometimes reputation was weighed, sometimes palace examination scripts were mined, sometimes special topic tests were set—again without uniform rule.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王儲才館閣以教養之。

translations.literal: Since antiquity emperors have stored talent in academy pavilions to nurture them.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity emperors have housed promising men in academy lodges to cultivate them.

sentences.zh: 本朝所以儲養之者，自及第進士之外，止有庶起士一途，而或選或否。

translations.literal: The way our dynasty nurtures them, apart from jinshi who have passed the examinations, has only the one path of expectant Hanlin scholars—and yet they may be chosen or not.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from jinshi who have completed the examination route, the dynasty relies chiefly on expectant Hanlin scholars to groom future ministers—yet even that track is optional.

sentences.zh: 且有才者未必皆選，所選者未必皆才，若更拘地方、年歲，則是已成之才又多棄而不用也。

translations.literal: Moreover, talented men are not necessarily all selected, and those selected are not necessarily all talented; if one further constrains by region and age, then many men already formed in talent are again abandoned and unused.
translations.idiomatic: Able men have been passed over while mediocre men have entered the academy; tighter limits on region and age would discard still more fully ripened talent.

sentences.zh: 請自今以後，立為定制，一次開科，一次選用。

translations.literal: I request that from now on it be established as a fixed regulation: each opening of the examinations, each selection and employment.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter each examination cycle be paired with one selection, as standing law.

sentences.zh: 令新進士錄平日所作論、策、詩、賦、序、記等文字，限十五篇以上，呈之禮部，送翰林考訂。

translations.literal: Let new jinshi record essays, policy papers, poems, fu, prefaces, records, and the like they have written in ordinary times, limited to fifteen pieces or more, present them to the Ministry of Rites, and send them to the Hanlin for evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: New jinshi should submit at least fifteen recent compositions—essays, policy papers, verse, fu, prefaces, and records—to the Ministry of Rites for forwarding to Hanlin review.

sentences.zh: 少年有新作五篇，亦許投試翰林院。

translations.literal: Young men with five new compositions are also permitted to submit them for trial at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Younger candidates with as few as five new pieces may also present them to the Hanlin for consideration.

sentences.zh: 擇其詞藻文理可取者，按號行取。

translations.literal: Those whose phrasing and literary pattern may be taken are taken in order by number.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates whose diction and structure qualify are admitted in roster order.

sentences.zh: 禮部以糊名試卷，偕閣臣出題考試於東閣，試卷與所投之文相稱，即收預選。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites sealed-name examination papers; together with grand secretaries they set topics and examined at the Eastern Lodge; when the examination papers matched the submitted writings, they were accepted into pre-selection.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry administered a sealed-name test with topics set by grand secretaries in the Eastern Lodge; men whose examination work matched their submitted portfolios entered the preliminary list.

sentences.zh: 每科所選不過二十人，每選所留不過三五輩，將來成就必有足賴者。」

translations.literal: Each cycle selects no more than twenty men, each selection retains no more than three or five cohorts; future achievements will surely have men enough to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: No cycle should pick more than twenty men, and no more than three to five cohorts should remain in training at once—enough to supply the state's future needs."

sentences.zh: 孝宗從其請，命內閣同吏、禮二部考選以為常。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong followed his request and ordered the inner cabinet together with the Ministries of Personnel and Rites to examine and select, making it regular.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hongzhi accepted the plan and made joint selection by the inner cabinet and the Personnel and Rites ministries standing practice.

sentences.zh: 自嘉靖癸未至萬曆庚辰，中間有九科不選。

translations.literal: From Jiajing guwei to Wanli gengchen, in the middle nine cycles did not select.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jiajing guwei cycle (1523) and Wanli gengchen (1600), nine cycles passed without a selection.

sentences.zh: 神宗常命間科一選。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong often ordered selection every other cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wanli repeatedly ordered selection every other examination.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎吳道南持不可。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Wu Daonan held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wu Daonan argued against it.

sentences.zh: 崇禎甲戌、丁丑，復不選，餘悉遵例。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen jiaxu and dingchou, again no selection; the remainder all followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen jiaxu (1634) and dingchou (1637) again saw none chosen; otherwise precedent was followed.

sentences.zh: 其與選者，謂之館選。

translations.literal: Those who entered selection were called academy selection.
translations.idiomatic: Those chosen were said to undergo academy selection.

sentences.zh: 以翰、詹官高資深者一人課之，謂之教習。

translations.literal: One senior Hanlin or Academician official of high standing instructed them, called instructor.
translations.idiomatic: A senior Hanlin or Academician served as instructor.

sentences.zh: 三年學成，優者留翰林為編修、檢討，次者出為給事、御史，謂之散館。

translations.literal: After three years of study the superior remained in the Hanlin as compiler or proofreader; the lesser went out as supervising secretaries or censors, called dispersal from the academy.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the best stayed in the Hanlin as compilers or proofreaders; the rest left for posts such as supervising secretary or censor—known as dispersal from the academy.

sentences.zh: 與常調官待選者，體格殊異。

translations.literal: Compared with regular-route officials awaiting selection, their status was quite distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Their standing differed sharply from ordinary officials awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 成祖初年，內閣七人，非翰林者居其半。

translations.literal: In the early years of Chengzu, seven men in the inner cabinet, and half were not Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chengzu's reign the inner cabinet had seven members, half of whom were not Hanlin men.

sentences.zh: 翰林纂修，亦諸色參用。

translations.literal: Hanlin compilers also drew on all sorts together.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin drafting likewise mixed many backgrounds.

sentences.zh: 自天順二年，李賢奏定纂修專選進士。

translations.literal: From the second year of Tianshun, Li Xian memorialized fixing compilation and revision to select exclusively jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 2 (1458) Li Xian restricted historical compilation to jinshi scholars.

sentences.zh: 由是非進士不入翰林，非翰林不入內閣，南、北禮部尚書、侍郎及吏部右侍郎，非翰林不任。

translations.literal: Henceforth, non-jinshi did not enter the Hanlin, non-Hanlin did not enter the inner cabinet; southern and northern Ministers of Rites and Vice Ministers, and the Vice Minister of Personnel on the right, were not appointed without Hanlin service.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter non-jinshi could not enter the Hanlin, non-Hanlin could not enter the inner cabinet, and the Rites ministers north and south, their deputies, and the right-hand Vice Minister of Personnel required Hanlin experience.

sentences.zh: 而庶起士始進之時，已羣目為儲相。

translations.literal: And when expectant Hanlin scholars first entered, they were already collectively regarded as reserve chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Expectant Hanlin scholars on first appointment were already treated as chancellors-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 通計明一代宰輔一百七十餘人，由翰林者十九。

translations.literal: Counting through the entire Ming, chief ministers and assistants numbered more than one hundred seventy; nineteen came by way of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Across the whole Ming dynasty, more than one hundred seventy men served as chief ministers or grand secretaries; nineteen came through the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 蓋科舉視前代為盛，翰林之盛，則前代所絕無也。

translations.literal: Generally the civil examinations compared with the previous dynasties were flourishing; the flourishing of the Hanlin was what the previous dynasties utterly lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Civil examinations had never been grander; the Hanlin's prominence was likewise without precedent.

sentences.zh: 輔臣子弟，國初少登第者。

translations.literal: Sons of assisting ministers, in the founding of the state few passed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early years, few sons of grand secretaries won degrees.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年，陳循、王文以其子北闈下第，力攻主考劉儼，臺省譁然論其失。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jingtai, Chen Xun and Wang Wen, because their sons failed the Shuntian provincial exam, forcefully attacked chief examiner Liu Yan; the censorate and ministries clamored discussing their error.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 7 (1456), Chen Xun and Wang Wen, whose sons had failed the Shuntian provincial exam, assailed chief examiner Liu Yan; censors and ministries rose in uproar at the abuse.

sentences.zh: 帝勉徇二人意，命其子一體會試，而心薄之。

translations.literal: The emperor reluctantly followed the two men's wishes, ordered their sons together to take the metropolitan exam, yet in heart held them in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grudgingly indulged them, allowing their sons to sit the metropolitan exam with the rest, but held the ministers in contempt.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，焦芳子黃中會試中式，芳引嫌不讀卷。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde, Jiao Fang's son Huang Zhong passed the metropolitan exam; Fang cited conflict of interest and did not read papers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 3 (1508), Jiao Fang's son Huang Zhong passed the metropolitan exam; Fang declined to grade papers on grounds of conflict.

sentences.zh: 而黃中居二甲之首，芳意猶不慊，至降調諸翰林以泄其忿。

translations.literal: Yet Huang Zhong stood first in the second grade; Fang's mind was still not satisfied, even demoting and transferring various Hanlin to vent his wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong ranked first in the second grade, yet Fang remained dissatisfied and demoted and transferred Hanlin scholars to vent his anger.

sentences.zh: 六年，楊廷和子慎廷試第一，廷和時亦引嫌不讀卷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yang Tinghe's son Shen was first in the palace exam; Tinghe at the time also cited conflict of interest and did not read papers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1511, Yang Shen, son of Yang Tinghe, topped the palace examination; Tinghe likewise abstained from grading.

sentences.zh: 慎以高才及第，人無訾之者。

translations.literal: Shen by high talent attained the degree; no man faulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's surpassing talent silenced criticism.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年廷試，翟鑾子汝儉、汝孝俱在試中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing palace exam, Zhai Luan's sons Rujian and Ruxiao were both among those examined.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiajing 23 (1544) palace examination, Zhai Luan's sons Rujian and Ruxiao both sat the test.

sentences.zh: 世宗疑二人濫首甲，抑第一為第三，以第三置三甲。

translations.literal: Shizong suspected the two men had wantonly taken top first grade; he suppressed the first to third, placing the third in the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected favoritism in the top ranks, demoting the first-placed candidate to third and the third to the bottom tier.

sentences.zh: 及拆卷，而所擬第三者，果汝孝也，帝大疑之。

translations.literal: When the papers were unsealed, the one proposed as third was indeed Ruxiao; the emperor greatly suspected it.
translations.idiomatic: When the papers were opened, the third-ranked manuscript proved to be Ruxiao's; the emperor's suspicions deepened.

sentences.zh: 給事中王交、王堯日因劾會試考官少詹事江汝璧及諸房考朋私通賄，且追論順天鄉試考官秦鳴夏、浦應麒阿附鑾罪，乃下汝璧等鎮撫司獄。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Wang Jiao and Wang Yaori thereupon impeached metropolitan exam chief examiner Junior Guardian Jiang Rubi and various room examiners for faction and bribery, and also pressed charges against Shuntian provincial examiners Qin Mingxia and Pu Yingqi for currying Zhai Luan's favor; they were then sent to the Imperial Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Wang Jiao and Wang Yaori impeached chief metropolitan examiner Jiang Rubi and associate examiners for collusion and bribery, and revived charges that Shuntian chief examiners Qin Mingxia and Pu Yingqi had favored Zhai Luan; the accused were sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 獄具，詔杖汝璧、鳴夏、應麒，並革職閑住，而勒鑾父子為民。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, an edict cane-flogged Rubi, Mingxia, and Yingqi, dismissed them all to idle residence, and compelled the Luan father and sons to become commoners.
translations.idiomatic: After trial, an edict ordered Jiang Rubi, Qin Mingxia, and Pu Yingqi beaten and cashiered to private life, and reduced the Zhai father and sons to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，張居正當國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenzong, Zhang Juzheng held the state.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenzong's reign, Zhang Juzheng dominated government.

sentences.zh: 二年甲戌，其子禮闈下第，居正不悅，遂不選庶起士。

translations.literal: In the second year jiaxu, his son failed the Ministry of Rites exam enclosure; Juzheng was displeased, and consequently did not select expectant Hanlin scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In 1574 his son failed the metropolitan exam; displeased, Juzheng suspended selection of expectant Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 至五年，其子嗣修遂以一甲第二人及第。

translations.literal: By the fifth year, his son Siziu then attained the degree as second man of the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: By 1577 his son Siziu had placed second in the top tier.

sentences.zh: 至八年，其子懋修以一甲第一人及第。

translations.literal: By the eighth year, his son Maoxiu attained the degree as first man of the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1580 his son Maoxiu took first place in the top tier.

sentences.zh: 而次輔呂調陽、張四維、申時行之子，亦皆先後成進士。

translations.literal: And the vice assisting ministers Lü Tiaoyang, Zhang Siwei, and Shen Shixing's sons also all in succession became jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of vice grand secretaries Lü Tiaoyang, Zhang Siwei, and Shen Shixing likewise passed the examinations in succession.

sentences.zh: 御史魏允貞疏陳時弊，言輔臣子不宜中式。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Yunzhen memorialized stating current abuses, saying assisting ministers' sons ought not to pass the exam.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Yunzhen memorialized on abuses of the day, arguing that grand secretaries' sons should not pass examinations.

sentences.zh: 帝為謫允貞。

translations.literal: The emperor on his behalf demoted Yunzhen.
