translations.idiomatic: The emperor banished Wei Yunzhen in reprisal.

sentences.zh: 十六年，右庶子黃洪憲主順天試，王錫爵子衡為榜首。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Right Sub-Reader Huang Hongxian presided over the Shuntian exam; Wang Xijue's son Heng was first on the list.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 16 (1588), Right Sub-Reader Huang Hongxian chief-examined Shuntian; Wang Xijue's son Heng ranked first.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中高桂論劾舉人李鴻等，並及衡，言：「自故相子一時並進，而大臣之子遂無見信於天下者。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites Director Gao Gui impeached and denounced candidates Li Hong and others, extending also to Heng, saying: "Since former chief ministers' sons advanced together at one time, thereafter chief ministers' sons have had no trust from the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry Director Gao Gui impeached candidates including Li Hong and extended his charges to Heng, writing: "Since the sons of former chief ministers rose together, no minister's son has enjoyed public trust.

sentences.zh: 今輔臣錫爵子衡，素號多才，青雲不難自致，而人猶疑信相半，宜一體覆試，以明大臣之心跡。」

translations.literal: Now assisting minister Xijue's son Heng, long known for manifold talent, high eminence not difficult to reach of himself, yet men still half doubt and half trust; it is fitting to re-examine all together to clarify the great minister's mind and track."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Xijue's gifted son Heng could surely rise on his own merits, yet the public remains divided; a comprehensive re-examination should clarify a great minister's integrity."

sentences.zh: 錫爵怒甚，具奏申辨，語過激。

translations.literal: Xijue was very angry, submitted a full memorial pleading his case, language excessively heated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue was furious, memorialized at length in self-defense with intemperate language.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事饒伸復抗疏論之。

translations.literal: Ministry of Justice clerk Rao Shen again submitted a defiant memorial discussing it.
translations.idiomatic: Justice Bureau clerk Rao Shen again memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 帝為謫桂於外，下伸獄，削其官。

translations.literal: The emperor on his behalf demoted Gui abroad, sent Shen to prison, stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exiled Gao Gui, imprisoned Rao Shen, and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 覆試所劾舉人，仍以衡第一，且無一人黜者。

translations.literal: On re-examination of the impeached candidates, still Heng was first, and moreover not one man was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Re-examination left Heng first and dismissed no candidate.

sentences.zh: 二十年會試，李鴻中式。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year metropolitan exam, Li Hong passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli 20 (1592) metropolitan examination Li Hong passed.

sentences.zh: 鴻，大學士申時行婿也。

translations.literal: Hong was Grand Secretary Shen Shixing's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was son-in-law to Grand Secretary Shen Shixing.

sentences.zh: 榜將發，房考給事中某持之，以為宰相之婿不當中。

translations.literal: As the list was about to be posted, a room examiner supervising secretary so-and-so held it back, thinking the chief minister's son-in-law ought not to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before the placard could be posted, one associate examiner, a supervising secretary, blocked it, arguing a chief minister's son-in-law should not pass.

sentences.zh: 主考官張位使十八房考公閱，皆言文字可取，而給事猶持不可。

translations.literal: Chief examiner Zhang Wei had the eighteen room examiners jointly review; all said the writing merited acceptance, yet the supervising secretary still held it could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Chief examiner Zhang Wei had all eighteen associates review jointly; all found the essays acceptable, yet the censor held firm.

sentences.zh: 位怒曰：「考試不憑文字，將何取衷？

translations.literal: Wei angrily said: "If the examination does not rely on the writing, on what shall one take the standard?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei snapped: "If examinations ignore the writing, what standard remains?

sentences.zh: 我請職其咎。」

translations.literal: I request to bear the blame."
translations.idiomatic: I will bear the blame myself."

sentences.zh: 鴻乃獲收。

translations.literal: Hong then obtained acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong was admitted.

sentences.zh: 王衡既被論，當錫爵在位，不復試禮闈。

translations.literal: Wang Heng having been impeached, while Xijue was in office, did not again try the Ministry of Rites exam enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: After the controversy Wang Heng did not sit the metropolitan examination while his father remained in power.

sentences.zh: 二十九年乃以一甲第二人及第。

translations.literal: Only in the twenty-ninth year did he attain the degree as second man of the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Only in 1601 did he place second in the top tier.

sentences.zh: 自後輔臣當國，其子亦無登第者矣。

translations.literal: From then on while assisting ministers held the state, their sons also had none who passed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter no grand secretary's son passed the examinations while his father held power.

sentences.zh: 科場弊竇既多，議論頻數。

translations.literal: Examination-hall malpractices being many, discussion was frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Malpractices multiplied and debate grew constant.

sentences.zh: 自太祖重罪劉三吾等，永、宣間大抵帖服。

translations.literal: Since Taizu heavily punished Liu Sanwu and others, between Yongle and Xuande periods men were largely compliant.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu punished Liu Sanwu and his colleagues, the Yongle and Xuande reigns were comparatively quiet.

sentences.zh: 陳循、王文之齮劉儼也，高穀持之，儼亦無恙。

translations.literal: When Chen Xun and Wang Wen bore hostility toward Liu Yan, Gao Gu stood firm for him, and Yan also came to no harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xun and Wang Wen assailed Liu Yan, Gao Gu defended him and Yan emerged unscathed.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年會試，大學士李東陽、少詹事程敏政為考官。

translations.literal: Hongzhi twelfth year metropolitan exam, Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and Junior Guardian Cheng Minzheng were examiners.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hongzhi 12 (1499) metropolitan examination Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and Junior Guardian Cheng Minzheng served as examiners.

sentences.zh: 給事中華昶劾敏政鬻題與舉人唐寅、徐泰，乃命東陽獨閱文字。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Hua Chang impeached Minzheng for selling topics to candidates Tang Yin and Xu Tai; the court then ordered Dongyang alone to review writings.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Hua Chang charged Minzheng with selling examination topics to candidates Tang Yin and Xu Tai; Dongyang alone was ordered to grade papers.

sentences.zh: 給事中林廷玉復攻敏政可疑者六事。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Lin Tingyu again attacked six doubtful matters concerning Minzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Lin Tingyu renewed the attack with six counts of suspicion against Minzheng.

sentences.zh: 敏政謫官，寅泰皆斥譴。

translations.literal: Minzheng was demoted in office; Yin and Tai were both dismissed and reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Minzheng was demoted; Yin and Tai were disgraced and sent away.

sentences.zh: 寅，江左才士，戊午南闈第一，論者多惜之。

translations.literal: Yin was a talent of the Jiangzuo region; in wuwu he was first in the southern provincial exam, and many in discussion regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, a brilliant Jiangnan scholar who had topped the southern provincial examination in 1498, was widely mourned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十六年，禮部尚書嚴嵩連摘應天、廣東試錄語，激世宗怒。

translations.literal: Jiajing sixteenth year, Minister of Rites Yan Song repeatedly picked out phrases from the Jiangnan and Guangdong examination records, provoking Shizong's anger.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 16 (1537) Minister Yan Song seized on phrasing in the Jiangnan and Guangdong examination reports and inflamed the emperor's wrath.

sentences.zh: 應天主考及廣東巡按御史俱逮問。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan chief examiner and the Guangdong touring censor were both arrested and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan chief examiner and Guangdong investigating censor were both arrested.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，帝手批山東試錄譏訕，逮御史葉經杖死闕下，佈政以下皆遠謫，亦嵩所中傷也。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, the emperor personally annotated the Shandong examination record as ridicule; censor Ye Jing was arrested and caned to death below the palace gate; provincial administration commissioners and below were all exiled far, also harm done by Song.
translations.idiomatic: In 1543 the emperor personally annotated the Shandong report as seditious; Censor Ye Jing was beaten to death at the palace gates and officials down to provincial commissioners were banished—again Yan Song's doing.

sentences.zh: 四十年，應天主考中允無錫吳情取同邑十三人，被劾，與副考胡傑俱謫外。

translations.literal: Fortieth year, Jiangnan chief examiner Sub-Reader from Wuxi Wu Qing took thirteen men of the same district; impeached, together with associate examiner Hu Jie both were demoted abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In 1561 Chief Examiner Wu Qing, subreader from Wuxi, admitted thirteen men from his native county and was impeached; he and associate examiner Hu Jie were both exiled.

sentences.zh: 南畿翰林遂不得典應天試矣。

translations.literal: Hanlin of the southern capital region thereafter could not preside over the Jiangnan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Southern-region Hanlin scholars were thereafter barred from examining Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年，順天主考高汝愚中張居正子嗣修、懋修，及居正黨吏部侍郎王篆子之衡、之鼎。

translations.literal: Wanli fourth year, Shuntian chief examiner Gao Ruyu passed Zhang Juzheng's sons Siziu and Maoxiu, and Juzheng's faction member Vice Minister of Personnel Wang Zhuan's sons Zhiheng and Zhiding.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 4 (1576), Shuntian chief examiner Gao Ruyu passed Zhang Juzheng's sons Siziu and Maoxiu plus sons of his ally Vice Minister Wang Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 居正既死，御史丁此呂追論其弊，且言：「汝愚以『舜亦以命禹』為試題，殆以禪受阿居正。」

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, censor Ding Cilü pursued discussion of the abuses, and also said: "Ruyu took 'Shun also entrusted Yu' as examination topic, roughly using abdication-through-merit to flatter Juzheng."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng died, Censor Ding Cilü pursued the scandal, noting that Gao Ruyu had set "Shun also entrusted Yu" as a topic—an apparent nod to succession by merit flattering Juzheng."

sentences.zh: 當國者惡此呂，謫於外，而議者多不直汝愚。

translations.literal: Those holding the state hated Cilü, demoted him abroad, yet many in discussion did not side with Ruyu.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power banished Ding Cilü, yet public opinion largely favored him over Gao Ruyu.

sentences.zh: 三十八年會試，庶子湯賓尹為同考官，與各房互換闈卷，共十八人。

translations.literal: Thirty-eighth year metropolitan exam, Sub-Reader Tang Binyin as associate examiner swapped examination-hall papers with each room, altogether eighteen men.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wanli 38 (1610) metropolitan examination Associate Examiner Tang Binyin swapped papers across eighteen candidates with various room examiners.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史孫居相劾賓尹私韓敬，其互換皆以敬故。

translations.literal: Next year, censor Sun Juxiang impeached Binyin for favoring Han Jing in private; all the swaps were for Jing's sake.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Censor Sun Juxiang charged that Binyin had favored Han Jing and that every swap served Jing.

sentences.zh: 時吏部方考察，尚書孫丕揚因置賓尹、敬於察典。

translations.literal: At the time the Ministry of Personnel was conducting inspection; Minister Sun Piyang thereupon placed Binyin and Jing in the inspection register.
translations.idiomatic: During the ministry's personnel review, Minister Sun Piyang placed Binyin and Jing on the evaluation roster.

sentences.zh: 敬頗有文名，眾亦惜敬，而以其宣黨，謂其宜斥也。

translations.literal: Jing had considerable literary fame; the multitude also regretted Jing, yet because he was of the Xuan faction, said he ought to be expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jing enjoyed literary renown and sympathy, yet as a member of the Xuan faction was judged fit for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 四十四年會試，吳江沈同和第一，同里趙鳴陽第六。

translations.literal: Forty-fourth year metropolitan exam, Wujiang Shen Tonghe first, fellow townsman Zhao Mingyang sixth.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli 44 (1616) metropolitan examination placed Wujiang's Shen Tonghe first and his townsman Zhao Mingyang sixth.

sentences.zh: 同和素不能文，文多出鳴陽手，事發覺，兩人並謫戍。

translations.literal: Tonghe by nature could not write; writings mostly came from Mingyang's hand; when the affair was discovered, both men were demoted to frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe could scarcely write; Zhao Mingyang ghost-wrote his papers; exposed, both were banished to border service.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，山東、江西、湖廣、福建考官，皆以策問譏刺，降諭切責。

translations.literal: Tianqi fourth year, Shandong, Jiangxi, Huguang, and Fujian examiners all because policy questions contained ridicule received descending edicts sternly reproaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 4 (1624), examiners in Shandong, Jiangxi, Huguang, and Fujian were sharply rebuked by edict when their policy questions were judged seditious.

sentences.zh: 初命貶調，既而褫革，江西主考丁乾學至下獄擬罪，蓋觸魏忠賢怒也。

translations.literal: At first ordered demoted and transferred, then stripped and dismissed; Jiangxi chief examiner Ding Qianxue even entered prison with sentence proposed, roughly having provoked Wei Zhongxian's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Initially demoted, then cashiered; Jiangxi chief examiner Ding Qianxue was imprisoned on proposed charges after offending Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 先是二年辛酉，中允錢謙益典試浙江，所取舉人錢千秋卷七篇大結，跡涉關節。

translations.literal: Earlier in the second year xinyou, Sub-Reader Qian Qianyi presided over Zhejiang examination; the candidate he took Qian Qianqiu's seven essays had large conclusions, traces involving examination-hall levers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in 1621 Sub-Reader Qian Qianyi examined Zhejiang and admitted Qian Qianqiu, whose seven essays bore telltale coded endings suggesting illicit coordination.

sentences.zh: 榜後為人所訐，謙益自檢舉，千秋謫戍。

translations.literal: After the list was posted someone impeached; Qianyi himself reported the matter; Qianqiu was demoted to frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After the results were posted someone reported the scheme; Qianyi confessed; Qianqiu was banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 未幾，赦還。

translations.literal: Before long, amnestied and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon amnestied and recalled.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年會推閣臣，謙益以禮部侍郎與焉，而尚書溫體仁不與。

translations.literal: Chongzhen second year joint recommendation for cabinet ministers, Qianyi as Vice Minister of Rites was included, yet Minister Wen Tiren was not.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 (1629), during joint nomination for grand secretary, Vice Minister Qian Qianyi was listed while Minister Wen Tiren was not.

sentences.zh: 體仁摘千秋事，出疏攻謙益。

translations.literal: Tiren picked out the Qianqiu affair, issued a memorial attacking Qianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren seized on the Qianqiu scandal and memorialized against Qian Qianyi.

sentences.zh: 謙益由此罷，遂終明世不復起。

translations.literal: Qianyi thereby was dismissed, and through the end of the Ming never rose again.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi was removed and never served again through the dynasty's end.

sentences.zh: 其他指摘科場事者，前後非一，往往北闈為甚，他省次之。

translations.literal: Other accusations of examination-hall matters, before and after not one, often the Shuntian exam was most severe, other provinces next.
translations.idiomatic: Other examination scandals were innumerable; Shuntian cases were usually worst, other provinces less so.

sentences.zh: 其賄買鑽營、懷挾倩代、割卷傳遞、頂名冒籍，弊端百出，不可窮究，而關節為甚。

translations.literal: Their bribery purchase, drilling for favor, carrying forbidden materials and hiring substitutes, cutting papers and passing them along, assuming names and false registration—abuses sprouted by the hundred, impossible to exhaust investigation, yet examination-hall levers were most severe.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery, manipulation, smuggled answers, hired substitutes, paper-switching, impersonation, and false registration proliferated beyond reckoning, yet coordinated inside control remained the gravest abuse.

sentences.zh: 事屬曖昧，或快恩仇報復，蓋亦有之。

translations.literal: Matters belonging to ambiguity, or settling favor and enmity in revenge, roughly also existed.
translations.idiomatic: Some cases arose from ambiguous evidence or private vendettas.

sentences.zh: 其他小小得失，無足道也。

translations.literal: Other small gains and losses are not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser irregularities hardly merit notice.

sentences.zh: 曆科事蹟稍異者：永樂初，兵革倉猝，元年癸未，始令各省鄉試。

translations.literal: Across examination cycles matters slightly unusual: early Yongle, military campaigns urgent; first year guwei, first ordered each province's provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Notable anomalies across the examinations: early Yongle, amid military upheaval, 1403 first authorized provincial examinations in every province.

sentences.zh: 二年甲申會試，以事變不循午未之舊。

translations.literal: Second year jiashen metropolitan exam, because of events did not follow the old wuwei and weiwei pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The 1404 metropolitan examination broke the usual biennial cycle because of the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 七年己丑會試，中陳燧等九十五人。

translations.literal: Seventh year jichou metropolitan exam passed Chen Sui and ninety-five others.
translations.idiomatic: The 1409 metropolitan examination passed ninety-five men including Chen Sui.

sentences.zh: 成祖方北征，皇太子令送國子監進學，俟車駕還京廷試。

translations.literal: Chengzu was on northern campaign; the heir apparent ordered them sent to the Directorate to advance studies, awaiting the imperial carriage's return to the capital for palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: With Chengzu campaigning in the north, the heir apparent sent them to the Imperial Academy to study pending the emperor's return for the palace exam.

sentences.zh: 九年辛卯，始擢蕭時中第一。

translations.literal: Ninth year xinmao, only then elevated Xiao Shizhong first.
translations.idiomatic: In 1411 Xiao Shizhong was finally named first.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年庚戌，帝臨軒發策畢，退禦武英殿，謂翰林儒臣曰：「取士不尚虛文，有若劉蕡、蘇轍輩直言抗論，朕當顯庸之。」

translations.literal: Xuande fifth year gengxu, when the emperor had finished issuing policy questions at the imperial presence and withdrew to the Wuying Hall, he told Hanlin Confucian officials: "In taking scholars do not esteem empty writings; if there were men like Liu Zan or Su Zhe who spoke straight and argued boldly, I would distinguish and employ them."
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 5 (1430), after issuing palace-examination questions the emperor told Hanlin scholars at the Wuying Hall: "Do not prize empty eloquence alone; men like Liu Zan or Su Zhe, who spoke plainly and argued forcefully, I would elevate."

sentences.zh: 乃賦《策士歌》以示讀卷官，顧所擢第一人林震，亦無所表見也。

translations.literal: He then composed "Song for Policy Scholars" to show the paper-reading officials; yet the first man he elevated, Lin Zhen, also had nothing to show.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the "Song for Examinees" for the graders, yet Lin Zhen, whom he placed first, distinguished himself no further.

sentences.zh: 八年癸丑，廷試第一人曹鼐，由江西泰和典史會試中式。

translations.literal: Eighth year guichou, palace examination first Cao Nai, from Jiangxi Taihe district magistrate's clerk, had passed metropolitan exam.
translations.idiomatic: In 1433 palace graduate Cao Nai, a petty clerk from Taihe in Jiangxi, had passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 正統七年壬戌，刑部吏南昱、公陵驛丞鄭溫亦皆中式。

translations.literal: Zhengtong seventh year renxu, Ministry of Justice clerk Nan Yu and Gongling post station assistant director Zheng Wen also all passed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 7 (1442) likewise saw a Justice Bureau clerk, Nan Yu, and a postal-station deputy, Zheng Wen, pass.

sentences.zh: 十年乙丑，會試、廷試第一皆商輅。

translations.literal: Tenth year yichou, metropolitan and palace examination first were both Shang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1445 both metropolitan and palace examinations placed Shang Lu first.

sentences.zh: 輅，淳安人，宣宗末年乙卯，浙榜第一人。

translations.literal: Lu was a Chun'an man; at the end of Xuande's reign in yimao he was first on the Zhejiang list.
translations.idiomatic: A native of Chun'an, he had topped the Zhejiang provincial list in 1435.

sentences.zh: 三試皆第一，士子豔稱為三元，明代惟輅一人而已。

translations.literal: All three examinations first, scholars gorgeously called it Triple First; in the Ming only Lu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Three consecutive first places earned him the coveted title "Triple First"; he alone in the Ming achieved it.

sentences.zh: 廷試讀卷盡用甲科，而是年兵部尚書徐晞、十三年戶部侍郎餘亨乃吏員，天順元年丁丑讀卷左都御史楊善乃譯字生，時猶未甚拘流品也。

translations.literal: Palace examination paper-reading wholly used top-grade graduates, yet that year Minister of War Xu Xi, thirteenth year Vice Minister of Revenue Yu Heng were clerical staff; Tianshun first year dingchou paper-reading Left Censor-in-Chief Yang Shan was a translation-bureau trainee—at the time they had not yet greatly constrained mixed streams.
translations.idiomatic: Palace examiners were usually top-tier graduates, yet in 1445 War Minister Xu Xi and in 1448 Revenue Vice Minister Yu Heng were clerical appointees, and in 1457 Left Censor-in-Chief Yang Shan, a translation-bureau trainee, read papers—rank was not yet rigidly enforced.

sentences.zh: 迨後無雜流會試及為讀卷官者矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter none of mixed stream passed metropolitan examination or served as paper-reading officials.
translations.idiomatic: Later no men of irregular background passed the metropolitan exam or graded palace papers.

sentences.zh: 七年癸未試日，場屋火，死者九十餘人，俱贈進士出身，改期八月會試。

translations.literal: Seventh year guwei on exam day, the examination compound caught fire; more than ninety died; all were granted posthumous jinshi status; the date was changed to eighth month for metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: On examination day in 1443 the hall burned and more than ninety candidates died; all were posthumously granted jinshi status and the metropolitan exam was rescheduled for the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 明年甲申三月，始廷試。

translations.literal: Next year third month jiashen, only then palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination was not held until the third month of 1444.

sentences.zh: 時英宗已崩，憲宗以大喪未逾歲，禦西角門策之。

translations.literal: At the time Yingzong had died; Xianzong because major mourning had not passed one year issued policy questions at the West Corner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong had died; within the mourning year Xianzong examined candidates at the West Corner Gate.

sentences.zh: 正德三年戊辰，太監劉瑾錄五十人姓名以示主司，因廣五十名之額。

translations.literal: Zhengde third year wuchen, eunuch Liu Jin recorded fifty men's names to show the chief examiners, and thereby expanded the quota by fifty names.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 3 (1508), eunuch Liu Jin supplied fifty names to the examiners and the quota was enlarged by fifty places.

sentences.zh: 十五年庚辰，武宗南巡，未及廷試。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year gengchen, Wuzong toured south, and did not reach palace examination in time.
translations.idiomatic: In 1520 the emperor's southern tour delayed the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 次年，世宗即位，五月禦西角門策之，擢楊維聰第一。

translations.literal: Next year Shizong ascended; fifth month at West Corner Gate issued policy questions; elevated Yang Weicong first.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after Shizong's accession, the exam was held at the West Corner Gate in the fifth month and Yang Weicong was named first.

sentences.zh: 而張璁即是榜進士也，六七年間，當國用事，權侔人主矣。

translations.literal: Yet Zhang Cong was also a jinshi of that list; within six or seven years holding the state and wielding affairs, power equaled the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong had been on that same roster; within six or seven years he dominated government with power rivaling the throne.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年己丑，帝親閱廷試卷，手批一甲羅洪先、楊名、歐陽德，二甲唐順之、陳束、任瀚六人對策，各加評獎。

translations.literal: Jiajing eighth year jichou, the emperor personally reviewed palace examination papers, hand-annotated top first grade Luo Hongxian, Yang Ming, Ouyang De, second grade Tang Shunzhi, Chen Shu, Ren Han six men's policy responses, each adding praise.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 8 (1529) the emperor personally read palace papers, annotating top-tier graduates Luo Hongxian, Yang Ming, and Ouyang De and six second-tier respondents including Tang Shunzhi, Chen Shu, and Ren Han with individual commendations.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊一清等遂選順之、束、瀚及胡經等共二十人為庶起士，疏其名上，請命官教習。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and others then selected Shunzhi, Shu, Han and Hu Jing and others altogether twenty men as expectant Hanlin scholars, memorializing their names upward, requesting ordered officials to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and colleagues nominated Tang Shunzhi, Chen Shu, Ren Han, Hu Jing, and seventeen others—twenty in all—as expectant Hanlin scholars and requested imperial instructors.

sentences.zh: 忽降諭云：「起士之選，祖宗舊制誠善。

translations.literal: Suddenly descended edict saying: "Selection of expectant scholars, the ancestral institution is truly good.
translations.idiomatic: An abrupt edict declared: "Selection of expectant Hanlin scholars embodied fine ancestral practice.

sentences.zh: 邇來大臣徇私選取，市恩立黨，於國無益，自今不必選留。

translations.literal: Recently great ministers have privately selected favor, sold kindness and formed factions, of no benefit to the state; from now on it is not necessary to select and retain.
translations.idiomatic: Lately ministers have chosen by private favor, trading patronage and forming factions to the state's harm; hereafter none need be retained.

sentences.zh: 唐順之等一切除授，吏、禮二部及翰林院會議以聞。」

translations.literal: Tang Shunzhi and others all received assignment of offices; Ministries of Personnel and Rites together with Hanlin Academy deliberated to report."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shunzhi and the rest were assigned posts outright; the Ministries of Personnel and Rites and the Hanlin Academy deliberated and reported."

sentences.zh: 尚書方獻夫等遂阿旨謂順之等不必留，並限翰林之額，侍讀、侍講、修撰各三員，編修、檢討各六員。

translations.literal: Minister Fang Xianfu and others then curried the intent saying Shunzhi and others need not remain, and also limited Hanlin quotas: Readers-in-waiting and Expositors-in-waiting, Compilers-in-chief each three posts; Compilers and Proofreaders each six posts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Fang Xianfu and colleagues toadied to the edict, declaring that Tang Shunzhi and the others need not remain, and capped Hanlin offices: three readers-in-waiting, three expositors-in-waiting, and three chief compilers; six compilers and six proofreaders each.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: Fixed as statute.
translations.idiomatic: This was enacted as permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 蓋順之等出張璁、霍韜門，而心以大禮之議為非，不肯趨附，璁心惡之。

translations.literal: Generally Shunzhi and others came from Zhang Cong and Huo Tao's gates, yet in heart held the Great Rites debate wrong and refused to hasten and attach; Cong's heart hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shunzhi and his circle were pupils of Zhang Cong and Huo Tao yet rejected the Great Rites controversy and refused to court their patrons; Zhang Cong loathed them.

sentences.zh: 璁又方欲中一清，故以立黨之說進，而故事由此廢。

translations.literal: Cong was also just then wishing to strike at Yiqing; therefore advanced the argument of forming factions, and the old practice was thereby abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong was also moving against Yang Yiqing and advanced the faction-building charge; the old practice died there.

sentences.zh: 迨十一年壬辰，已罷館選，至九月復舉行之。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year renchen, academy selection had been abolished; in the ninth month it was carried out again.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven (1532) academy selection had been suspended; in the ninth month it was revived.

sentences.zh: 十四年乙未，帝親制策問，手自批閱，擢韓應龍第一。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year yiwei, the emperor personally composed the policy questions, annotated the papers with his own hand, and elevated Han Yinglong to first place.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen (1535) the emperor composed the policy questions himself, annotated the papers, and placed Han Yinglong first.

sentences.zh: 降諭論一甲三人及二甲第一名次前後之由。

translations.literal: An edict was issued explaining the reasons for the order of the three first-cohort men and the first man of the second cohort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict explained why the first cohort and the leader of the second cohort were ranked as they were.

sentences.zh: 禮部因以聖諭列登科錄之首，而十二人對策，俱以次刊刻。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites therefore placed the imperial edict at the head of the roster of graduates, and the twelve men's policy answers were all printed in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites printed the imperial edict at the head of the graduates' roster and published all twelve policy answers in rank order.

sentences.zh: 二十年辛丑，考選庶起士題，文曰《原政》，詩曰《讀大明律》，皆欽降也。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year xinchou, topics for selecting expectant Hanlin scholars: the essay was "Origins of Government," the poem "Reading the Great Ming Code"—all were bestowed from on high.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty (1541) the examination topics for expectant Hanlin scholars were imperially assigned: the essay "Origins of Government" and the poem "Reading the Great Ming Code."

sentences.zh: 四十四年乙丑廷試，帝始不禦殿。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year yichou at the palace examination, the emperor for the first time did not attend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination in year forty-four (1565) the emperor for the first time did not preside in the hall.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，禦殿益稀矣。

translations.literal: In Shenzong's time, attendance in the hall grew ever rarer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong, imperial attendance at the palace examination became increasingly rare.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年壬戌會試，命大學士何宗彥、硃國祚為主考。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi renxu at the metropolitan examination, Grand Secretaries He Zongyan and Zhu Guozuo were ordered as chief examiners.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianqi 2 (1622) metropolitan examination Grand Secretaries He Zongyan and Zhu Guozuo were appointed chief examiners.

sentences.zh: 故事，閣臣典試，翰、詹一人副之。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a cabinet minister presided over the examination, one Hanlin or Academician assisted.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent a cabinet minister who examined was assisted by one Hanlin or Academician.

sentences.zh: 時已推禮部尚書顧秉謙，特旨命國祚。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Rites Gu Bingqian had already been nominated, but a special edict appointed Guozuo.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Gu Bingqian had already been nominated, but a special edict named Zhu Guozuo instead.

sentences.zh: 國祚疏辭，帝曰：「今歲，朕首科，特用二輔臣以光重典，卿不必辭。」

translations.literal: Guozuo memorialized to decline; the emperor said: "This year is my first examination cycle; I specially employ two assisting ministers to glorify this weighty rite—you need not decline."
translations.idiomatic: Guozuo declined in a memorial; the emperor replied: "This is my first examination season. I have specially appointed two grand secretaries to honor the occasion—you need not decline."

sentences.zh: 嗣後二輔臣典試以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter two assisting ministers examining became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it became standard for two grand secretaries to serve as chief examiners.

sentences.zh: 是年開宗科，硃慎鷸成進士，從宗彥、國祚請，即授中書舍人。

translations.literal: That year the imperial-clan examination was opened; Zhu Shenyu passed as jinshi, and at Zongyan and Guozuo's request was at once appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: That year the imperial-clan examination was held; Zhu Shenyu passed and, at He Zongyan and Zhu Guozuo's request, was immediately made a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，硃統飾成進士，初選庶起士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, Zhu Tongshi passed as jinshi and was first selected as an expectant Hanlin scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 4 (1631) Zhu Tongshi passed as jinshi and was first chosen as an expectant Hanlin scholar.

sentences.zh: 吏部以統飾宗室，不宜官禁近，請改中書舍人。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel, because Tongshi was imperial clansmen, said he was unsuited to office within the Forbidden City and asked that he be changed to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel argued that as imperial clansmen he should not hold office inside the Forbidden City and asked that he be made a Secretariat drafter instead.

sentences.zh: 統飾疏爭，命仍授庶起士。

translations.literal: Tongshi memorialized in protest; he was ordered still to receive appointment as expectant Hanlin scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Tongshi protested in a memorial and was nevertheless confirmed as an expectant Hanlin scholar.

sentences.zh: 七年甲戌，知貢舉禮部侍郎林釺言，舉人顏茂猷文兼《五經》，作二十三義。

translations.literal: In the seventh year jiaxu, Vice Minister of Rites in charge of the tribute examination Lin Qian reported that Presented Scholar Yan Maoyou's essays covered all Five Classics, producing twenty-three expositions.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven (1634) Vice Minister Lin Qian, who oversaw the examination, reported that Presented Scholar Yan Maoyou had written twenty-three classical expositions spanning all Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 帝念其該洽，許送內簾。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his comprehensive mastery, permitted him to be sent into the inner curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed by his breadth of learning, allowed his papers into the inner examination hall.

sentences.zh: 茂猷中副榜，特賜進士，以其名另為一行，刻於試錄第一名之前。

translations.literal: Maoyou passed on the supplementary list; he was specially granted jinshi status, and his name was set on a separate line engraved before the first name on the examination record.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyou placed on the supplementary list and was specially granted jinshi; his name was printed on its own line before the top-ranked candidate on the examination roster.

sentences.zh: 《五經》中式者，自此接跡矣。

translations.literal: Those who passed on all Five Classics followed one after another from this point.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who passed on all Five Classics thereafter appeared in succession.

sentences.zh: 武科，自吳元年定。

translations.literal: The military examination track was fixed from the first year of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The military examination system was established in the first year of the Wu reign.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十年俞禮部請，立武學，用武舉。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Hongwu, at the Ministry of Rites' request, a military academy was established and military Presented Scholars were used.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 20 (1387) the Ministry of Rites petitioned to establish a military academy and recruit through military examinations.

sentences.zh: 武臣子弟於各直省應試。

translations.literal: Sons of military officials sat the examinations in each metropolitan province and province.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of military officials were examined in each province.

sentences.zh: 天順八年，令天下文武官舉通曉兵法、謀勇出眾者，各省撫、按、三司，直隸巡按御史考試。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianshun, civil and military officials throughout the realm were ordered to recommend men versed in military strategy and outstanding in counsel and courage; in each province the grand coordinator, surveillance commissioner, and three offices, and in the metropolitan region the touring censor, examined them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 8 (1464) officials empire-wide were told to recommend men skilled in strategy and outstanding in courage; in the provinces the grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and three offices, and in the metropolitan region the touring censors, examined them.

sentences.zh: 中式者，兵部同總兵官于帥府試策略，教場試弓馬。

translations.literal: Those who passed were tested on strategy at the commander's headquarters jointly by the Ministry of War and the regional commander, and on bow and horse at the drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed were tested on strategy at headquarters with the regional commander and on archery and horsemanship at the drill ground.

sentences.zh: 答策二道，騎中四矢、步中二矢以上者為中式。

translations.literal: Two policy answers; hitting four arrows from horseback and two on foot or more counted as passing.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates answered two policy questions; passing required four hits on horseback and at least two on foot.

sentences.zh: 騎、步所中半焉者次之。

translations.literal: Those who hit half that number in riding and foot archery ranked next.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hit half as many ranked next.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年，從太監汪直請，設武科鄉、會試，悉視文科例。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua, following eunuch Wang Zhi's request, military provincial and metropolitan examinations were established, all following the civil model.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 14 (1478), at eunuch Wang Zhi's request, military provincial and metropolitan examinations were instituted on the civil model.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年，定武舉六歲一行，先策略，後弓馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi, military examinations were fixed every six years, strategy first, then bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 6 (1493) military examinations were set every six years, with strategy before archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 策不中者不許騎射。

translations.literal: Those who failed the policy section were not permitted the riding and shooting test.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who failed the written policy section could not proceed to archery.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改定三年一試，出榜賜宴。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year it was changed to once every three years, with placards posted and banquets granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen the cycle was changed to every three years, with published results and celebratory banquets.

sentences.zh: 正德十四年定，初場試馬上箭，以三十五步為則；

translations.literal: Fixed in the fourteenth year of Zhengde: the first session tested arrows on horseback at thirty-five paces as the standard;
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde 14 (1519) the first session tested mounted archery at thirty-five paces;

sentences.zh: 二場試步下箭，以八十步為則；

translations.literal: the second session tested arrows on foot at eighty paces as the standard;
translations.idiomatic: the second tested foot archery at eighty paces;

sentences.zh: 三場試策一道。

translations.literal: the third session tested one policy question.
translations.idiomatic: and the third set one policy question.

sentences.zh: 子、午、卯、酉年鄉試。

translations.literal: Provincial examinations were held in the years of zi, wu, mao, and you.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial military examinations fell in the years of the Rat, Horse, Rabbit, and Rooster.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，定制，各省應武舉者，巡按御史於十月考試，兩京武學於兵部選取，俱送兵部。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing the system was fixed: military candidates in each province were examined in the tenth month by the touring censor; the two capitals' military academies selected men at the Ministry of War—all were sent to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing the rules were set: provincial military candidates were examined in the tenth month by touring censors; the capital military academies selected candidates through the Ministry of War, and all were forwarded to that ministry.

sentences.zh: 次年四月會試，翰林二員為考試官，給事中、部曹四員為同考。

translations.literal: The following year in the fourth month was the metropolitan examination: two Hanlin men as chief examiners, four supervising secretaries and ministry officials as associates.
translations.idiomatic: The following April the metropolitan examination used two Hanlin examiners and four supervising secretaries or ministry officials as associates.

sentences.zh: 鄉、會場期俱於月之初九、十二、十五。

translations.literal: Provincial and metropolitan sessions were all on the ninth, twelfth, and fifteenth days of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and metropolitan sessions were held on the ninth, twelfth, and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 起送考驗監試張榜，大率仿文闈而減殺之。

translations.literal: Forwarding candidates, testing, supervising examinations, and posting results largely imitated the civil examination compound but in reduced form.
translations.idiomatic: Procedures for forwarding candidates, testing, supervision, and posting results largely followed the civil examinations in simplified form.

sentences.zh: 其後倏罷倏復。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was suddenly abolished and suddenly restored.
translations.idiomatic: The system was repeatedly suspended and restored.

sentences.zh: 又仿文闈南北卷例，分邊方、腹裏。

translations.literal: It also imitated the civil examination's north-south roll precedent, dividing frontier regions and the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Following the civil examination's north-south roll model, candidates were divided between frontier and interior regions.

sentences.zh: 每十名，邊六腹四以為常。

translations.literal: For every ten places, six frontier and four interior was the rule.
translations.idiomatic: The standard quota was six frontier candidates and four from the interior for every ten places.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十八年，定會試之額，取中進士以百名為率。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Wanli, the metropolitan quota was fixed at one hundred jinshi as the rate.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 38 (1610) the metropolitan military quota was fixed at one hundred jinshi.

sentences.zh: 其後有奉詔增三十名者，非常制也。

translations.literal: Later when thirty extra were granted by imperial edict, this was not the regular system.
translations.idiomatic: Later additions of thirty places by imperial edict were exceptions to the rule.

sentences.zh: 穆、神二宗時，議者嘗言武科當以技勇為重。

translations.literal: In the times of Muzong and Shenzong, discussants often said the military examination should stress skill and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Longqing and Wanli emperors critics often argued that military examinations should prioritize martial skill and courage.

sentences.zh: 萬曆之末，科臣又請特設將材武科，初場試馬步箭及槍、刀、劍、戟、拳搏、擊刺等法，二場試營陣、地雷、火藥、戰車等項，三場各就其兵法、天文、地理所熟知者言之。

translations.literal: At the end of Wanli, examination officials again asked to establish a special military track for general talent: the first session to test mounted and foot arrows and methods of spear, blade, sword, halberd, boxing, and thrusting; the second to test camp formations, land mines, gunpowder, war chariots, and the like; the third for each man to speak on military methods, astronomy, and geography he knew well.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wanli examination officials petitioned for a special track for military commanders: the first session would test mounted and foot archery plus spear, sword, halberd, and hand-to-hand skills; the second formations, mines, gunpowder, and war wagons; the third would let candidates discourse on strategy, astronomy, and geography they knew best.

sentences.zh: 報可而未行也。

translations.literal: The reply was approval, but it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal but never implemented it.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，武會試榜發，論者大嘩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, when the military metropolitan placard was issued, commentators were in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen 4 (1631) military metropolitan results were posted, public outcry was fierce.

sentences.zh: 帝命中允方逢年、倪元璐再試，取翁英等百二十人。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Sub-Readers Fang Fengnian and Ni Yuanlu to examine again, taking Weng Ying and one hundred twenty others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Sub-Readers Fang Fengnian and Ni Yuanlu to re-examine candidates and passed one hundred twenty men including Weng Ying.

sentences.zh: 逢年、元璐以時方需才，奏請殿試傳臚，悉如文例。

translations.literal: Fengnian and Yuanlu, because the time urgently needed talent, memorialized requesting a hall examination and announcement of ranks, all following the civil precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Fengnian and Yuanlu, citing the empire's urgent need for talent, petitioned for a palace examination and rank announcement on the civil model.

sentences.zh: 乃賜王來聘等及第、出身有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Laipin and others were granted immediate appointment and jinshi status with differences in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Laipin and others were then granted jinshi degrees and appointments according to rank.

sentences.zh: 武舉殿試自此始也。

translations.literal: The military examination hall test began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: The palace examination for military graduates dates from this occasion.

sentences.zh: 十四年，諭各部臣特開奇謀異勇科。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the various ministries were instructed specially to open an examination track for extraordinary stratagems and unusual courage.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen ministries were ordered to open a special examination for men of extraordinary strategy and courage.

sentences.zh: 詔下，無應者。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, no one responded.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, no one came forward.
